```
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import argparse
6	import json
7	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass

10	from artagents._paths import REPO_ROOT
11	from artagents.core.element.cli import _sync_managed_defaults
12	from artagents.core.element.install import install_element
13	from artagents.core.element.registry import load_default_registry as load_element_registry
14	
15	
16	@dataclass(frozen=True)
17	class SetupStep:
18	    name: str
19	    status: str
20	    detail: str
21	
22	
23	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
24	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python3 -m artagents setup", description="Plan or apply ArtAgents local setup.")
25	    parser.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true", help="Apply local setup mutations. Default is dry-run.")
26	    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit machine-readable setup output.")
27	    return parser
28	
29	
30	def plan_setup(*, apply: bool = False, project_root: str | Path | None = None) -> tuple[SetupStep, ...]:
31	    root = Path(project_root or REPO_ROOT)
32	    steps: list[SetupStep] = []
33	    steps.append(
34	        SetupStep(
35	            name="mode",
36	            status="apply" if apply else "dry-run",
37	            detail="local mutations enabled" if apply else "no files or dependencies will be changed",
38	        )
39	    )
40	    steps.append(_plan_agents_symlink(root, apply=apply))
41	    for action in _sync_managed_defaults(dry_run=not apply, overwrite=False, project_root=root):
42	        steps.append(SetupStep(name="elements sync", status="applied" if apply else "planned", detail=action))
43	
44	    registry = load_element_registry(project_root=root)
45	    for element in registry.list():
46	        result = install_element(element, project_root=root, dry_run=not apply)
47	        plan = result.plan
48	        if plan.noop_reason:
49	            steps.append(SetupStep(name="elements install", status="skipped", detail=f"{element.kind}/{element.id}: {plan.noop_reason}"))
50	            continue
51	        status = "applied" if apply else "planned"
52	        details = "; ".join(plan.command_lines())
53	        steps.append(SetupStep(name="elements install", status=status, detail=f"{element.kind}/{element.id}: {details}"))
54	    return tuple(steps)
55	
56	
57	def _plan_agents_symlink(root: Path, *, apply: bool) -> SetupStep:
58	    """Ensure AGENTS.md is a symlink to SKILL.md so both loaders read the same source."""
59	    agents = root / "AGENTS.md"
60	    target = "SKILL.md"
61	    skill = root / target
62	    if not skill.is_file():
63	        return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="warn", detail=f"{skill} missing; cannot link AGENTS.md")
64	    if agents.is_symlink() and (root / agents.readlink()).resolve() == skill.resolve():
65	        return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="ok", detail=f"AGENTS.md → {target}")
66	    if not agents.exists() and not agents.is_symlink():
67	        if apply:
68	            agents.symlink_to(target)
69	            return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="applied", detail=f"created AGENTS.md → {target}")
70	        return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="planned", detail=f"will create AGENTS.md → {target}")
71	    kind = "wrong symlink" if agents.is_symlink() else "regular file"
72	    if apply:
73	        agents.unlink()
74	        agents.symlink_to(target)
75	        return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="applied", detail=f"replaced AGENTS.md ({kind}) with symlink → {target}")
76	    return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="planned", detail=f"will replace AGENTS.md ({kind}) with symlink → {target}")
77	
78	
79	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
80	    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
81	    steps = plan_setup(apply=bool(args.apply))
82	    if args.json:
83	        payload = {
84	            "applied": bool(args.apply),
85	            "steps": [asdict(step) for step in steps],
86	        }
87	        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
88	        return 0
89	
90	    print("ArtAgents setup")
91	    if not args.apply:
92	        print("dry-run: pass --apply to sync managed defaults and run local element install commands")
93	    for step in steps:
94	        print(f"[{step.status}] {step.name}: {step.detail}")
95	    return 0
96	
97	
98	if __name__ == "__main__":
99	    raise SystemExit(main())
100
```

```
43	@dataclass(frozen=True)
44	class StructureReport:
45	    errors: tuple[str, ...]

47	    @property
48	    def ok(self) -> bool:

51	
52	def validate_repo_structure(root: str | Path = REPO_ROOT) -> StructureReport:
53	    repo_root = Path(root)
54	    errors: list[str] = []
55	    errors.extend(_validate_legacy_dirs(repo_root))
56	    errors.extend(_validate_local_state_dirs(repo_root))
57	    errors.extend(_validate_top_level_artagents(repo_root / "artagents"))
58	    errors.extend(_validate_executor_folders(repo_root / "artagents" / "executors"))
59	    errors.extend(_validate_orchestrator_folders(repo_root / "artagents" / "orchestrators"))
60	    return StructureReport(errors=tuple(errors))

62	
63	def _validate_legacy_dirs(repo_root: Path) -> list[str]:
64	    errors: list[str] = []
65	    for dirname in LEGACY_PUBLIC_DIRS:
66	        candidate = repo_root / "artagents" / dirname
67	        if candidate.exists():
68	            errors.append(f"legacy public package must not exist: {candidate.relative_to(repo_root)}")
69	    return errors
70	
71	
72	def _validate_local_state_dirs(repo_root: Path) -> list[str]:
73	    errors: list[str] = []
74	    local_root = repo_root / ".artagents"
75	    if not local_root.exists():
76	        return errors
77	    for dirname in LEGACY_LOCAL_DIRS:
78	        candidate = local_root / dirname
79	        if candidate.exists():
80	            errors.append(f"legacy local state directory must not exist: {candidate.relative_to(repo_root)}")
81	    return errors
82	
83	
84	def _validate_top_level_artagents(package_root: Path) -> list[str]:
85	    errors: list[str] = []
86	    for child in sorted(package_root.iterdir()):
87	        if child.name.startswith("."):
88	            continue
89	        if child.is_file() and child.suffix == ".py" and child.name not in TOP_LEVEL_ARTAGENTS_FILES:
90	            errors.append(f"top-level artagents module must move to a canonical package: {child.relative_to(package_root.parents[0])}")
91	        if child.is_dir() and child.name not in TOP_LEVEL_ARTAGENTS_DIRS:
92	            errors.append(f"top-level artagents directory is not a canonical concept: {child.relative_to(package_root.parents[0])}")
93	    return errors
94	
95	
96	def _validate_executor_folders(executors_root: Path) -> list[str]:
97	    if not executors_root.is_dir():
98	        return [f"missing executors directory: {executors_root}"]
99	
100	    errors: list[str] = []
101	    for folder in _public_child_dirs(executors_root, INTERNAL_EXECUTOR_DIRS):
102	        errors.extend(_require_files(folder, ("executor.yaml", "run.py", "STAGE.md"), root=executors_root.parents[1]))
103	        if _has_any(folder, ("orchestrator.yaml", "orchestrator.yml", "orchestrator.json", "orchestrator.py")):
104	            errors.append(f"executor folder contains orchestrator metadata: {folder.relative_to(executors_root.parents[1])}")
105	        try:
106	            definitions = load_folder_executors(folder)
107	        except Exception as exc:
108	            errors.append(f"invalid executor folder {folder.relative_to(executors_root.parents[1])}: {exc}")
109	            continue
110	        if not definitions:
111	            errors.append(f"executor folder emitted no executor metadata: {folder.relative_to(executors_root.parents[1])}")
112	            continue
113	        for definition in definitions:
114	            if definition.kind == "built_in" and definition.id.startswith("builtin."):
115	                expected = f"builtin.{folder.name}"
116	                if definition.id != expected:
117	                    errors.append(f"built-in executor {definition.id!r} must live in artagents/executors/{definition.id.removeprefix('builtin.')}")
118	            elif definition.kind == "external" and definition.id.startswith("external."):
119	                package = definition.metadata.get("package_id") or definition.id.removeprefix("external.").split(".", 1)[0]
120	                if package != folder.name:
121	                    errors.append(f"external executor {definition.id!r} package {package!r} must live in artagents/executors/{package}")
122	    return errors
123	
124	
125	def _validate_orchestrator_folders(orchestrators_root: Path) -> list[str]:
126	    if not orchestrators_root.is_dir():
127	        return [f"missing orchestrators directory: {orchestrators_root}"]
128	
129	    errors: list[str] = []
130	    for folder in _public_child_dirs(orchestrators_root, INTERNAL_ORCHESTRATOR_DIRS):
131	        errors.extend(_require_files(folder, ("orchestrator.yaml", "run.py", "STAGE.md"), root=orchestrators_root.parents[1]))
132	        if _has_any(folder, ("executor.yaml", "executor.yml", "executor.json", "executor.py")):
133	            errors.append(f"orchestrator folder contains executor metadata: {folder.relative_to(orchestrators_root.parents[1])}")
134	        try:
135	            definitions = load_folder_orchestrators(folder)
136	        except Exception as exc:
137	            errors.append(f"invalid orchestrator folder {folder.relative_to(orchestrators_root.parents[1])}: {exc}")
138	            continue
139	        if not definitions:
140	            errors.append(f"orchestrator folder emitted no orchestrator metadata: {folder.relative_to(orchestrators_root.parents[1])}")
141	            continue
142	        for definition in definitions:
143	            expected = f"builtin.{folder.name}"
144	            if definition.kind != "built_in" or definition.id != expected:
145	                errors.append(f"built-in orchestrator folder {folder.name!r} must expose id {expected!r}")
146	    return errors
147	
148	
149	def _public_child_dirs(root: Path, skipped: set[str]) -> tuple[Path, ...]:
150	    return tuple(sorted(path for path in root.iterdir() if path.is_dir() and path.name not in skipped and not path.name.startswith(".")))
151	
152	
153	def _require_files(folder: Path, filenames: tuple[str, ...], *, root: Path) -> list[str]:
154	    return [f"{folder.relative_to(root)} missing {filename}" for filename in filenames if not (folder / filename).is_file()]
155	
156	
157	def _has_any(folder: Path, filenames: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
158	    return any((folder / filename).exists() for filename in filenames)
159	
160	
161	__all__ = ["StructureReport", "validate_repo_structure"]
```

```
13	class OrchestratorSpec:
14	    """Small code-first wrapper that normalizes to `OrchestratorDefinition`."""
15	
16	    __slots__ = ("_definition",)
17	
18	    def __init__(
19	        self,
20	        *,
21	        id: str,
22	        name: str,
23	        runtime: RuntimeSpec | dict[str, Any],
24	        kind: str = "external",
25	        version: str = "0.1.0",
26	        description: str = "",
27	        inputs: tuple[Port | dict[str, Any], ...] | list[Port | dict[str, Any]] = (),
28	        outputs: tuple[Output | dict[str, Any], ...] | list[Output | dict[str, Any]] = (),
29	        child_executors: tuple[str, ...] | list[str] = (),
30	        child_orchestrators: tuple[str, ...] | list[str] = (),
31	        cache: CachePolicy | dict[str, Any] | None = None,
32	        isolation: IsolationMetadata | dict[str, Any] | None = None,
33	        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
34	    ) -> None:
35	        raw: dict[str, Any] = {
36	            "id": id,
37	            "name": name,
38	            "kind": kind,
39	            "version": version,
40	            "runtime": _to_plain(runtime),
41	            "inputs": [_to_plain(input_) for input_ in inputs],
42	            "outputs": [_to_plain(output) for output in outputs],
43	            "child_executors": list(child_executors),
44	            "child_orchestrators": list(child_orchestrators),
45	            "metadata": dict(metadata or {}),
46	        }
47	        if description:
48	            raw["description"] = description
49	        if cache is not None:
50	            raw["cache"] = _to_plain(cache)
51	        if isolation is not None:
52	            raw["isolation"] = _to_plain(isolation)
53	        self._definition = validate_orchestrator_definition(raw)
54	
55	    @classmethod
56	    def from_definition(cls, definition: OrchestratorDefinition | dict[str, Any]) -> "OrchestratorSpec":
57	        spec = cls.__new__(cls)
58	        spec._definition = validate_orchestrator_definition(definition)
59	        return spec
60	
61	    def to_definition(self) -> OrchestratorDefinition:
62	        return self._definition
63	
64	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
65	        return self._definition.to_dict()
66	
67	    def to_json(self, *, indent: int | None = 2) -> str:
68	        return self._definition.to_json(indent=indent)
69	
70	    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
71	        return getattr(self._definition, name)

74	def orchestrator(spec: OrchestratorSpec | OrchestratorDefinition | dict[str, Any] | None = None, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
75	    """Create a orchestrator spec or decorate a callable with validated metadata."""
76	
77	    resolved = OrchestratorSpec(**kwargs) if spec is None else _to_spec(spec)
78	
79	    def decorate(target: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[..., Any]:
80	        target.orchestrator = resolved.to_definition()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
81	        target.ORCHESTRATOR = resolved.to_definition()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
82	        return target
83	
84	    return decorate if kwargs or spec is not None else resolved
85	
86	
87	def _to_spec(value: OrchestratorSpec | OrchestratorDefinition | dict[str, Any]) -> OrchestratorSpec:
88	    if isinstance(value, OrchestratorSpec):
89	        return value
90	    return OrchestratorSpec.from_definition(value)
91	
92	
93	def _to_plain(value: Any) -> Any:
94	    if isinstance(value, OrchestratorSpec):
95	        return value.to_dict()
96	    if isinstance(value, OrchestratorDefinition):
97	        return value.to_dict()
98	    if isinstance(value, RuntimeSpec):
99	        return value.to_dict() if hasattr(value, "to_dict") else _drop_blank_defaults(asdict(value))
100	    if isinstance(value, CommandSpec):
101	        return _drop_blank_defaults(asdict(value))
102	    if is_dataclass(value):
103	        return _drop_blank_defaults(asdict(value))
104	    return value
105	
106	
107	def _drop_blank_defaults(value: Any) -> Any:
108	    if isinstance(value, dict):
109	        return {
110	            [REDACTED](item)
111	            for key, item in value.items()
112	            if item is not None and item != ""
113	        }
114	    if isinstance(value, list):
115	        return [_drop_blank_defaults(item) for item in value]
116	    if isinstance(value, tuple):
117	        return tuple(_drop_blank_defaults(item) for item in value)
118	    return value
```

```
48	def _load_env_var(name: str, env_file: Path | None) -> str:
49	    import os
50	
51	    value = os.environ.get(name, "").strip()
52	    if value:
53	        return value
54	    tried: list[str] = [f"{name} environment variable"]
55	    for candidate in _candidate_env_files(env_file):
56	        tried.append(str(candidate))
57	        if value := _read_env_value(candidate, name):
58	            return value
59	    raise SystemExit(f"{name} not found. Tried: {', '.join(tried)}")

62	def write_json(path: Path, payload: Any) -> None:
63	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
64	    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

67	def parse_image_size(value: str) -> str | dict[str, int]:
68	    if value in FAL_PRESETS:
69	        return value
70	    match = re.fullmatch(r"([1-9][0-9]*)x([1-9][0-9]*)", value.strip())
71	    if not match:
72	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
73	            "image-size must be a fal preset (square_hd, portrait_16_9, ...) or WIDTHxHEIGHT"
74	        )
75	    return {"width": int(match.group(1)), "height": int(match.group(2))}
```

```
202	def load_config(path_text: str) -> dict:
203	    path = Path(path_text).expanduser().resolve()
204	    if not path.is_file():
205	        usage_error(f"artagents: config file not found: {path}")
206	    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
207	    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
208	    if suffix == ".json":
209	        try:
210	            data = json.loads(text)
211	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
212	            usage_error(f"artagents: invalid JSON config {path}: {exc.msg}")
213	    elif suffix in {".yaml", ".yml"}:
214	        if yaml is None:
215	            usage_error(f"artagents: YAML config requires PyYAML: {path}")
216	        try:
217	            data = yaml.safe_load(text)
218	        except Exception as exc:
219	            usage_error(f"artagents: invalid YAML config {path}: {exc}")
220	    else:
221	        try:
222	            data = json.loads(text)
223	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
224	            if yaml is None:
225	                usage_error(f"artagents: unsupported config format for {path}; use JSON or install PyYAML for YAML")
226	            try:
227	                data = yaml.safe_load(text)
228	            except Exception as exc:
229	                usage_error(f"artagents: invalid config {path}: {exc}")
230	    if data is None:
231	        return {}
232	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
233	        usage_error(f"artagents: config must decode to an object: {path}")
234	    return data

236	
237	def normalize_config(raw: dict) -> dict:
238	    data = dict(raw)
239	    if "from" in data and "from_step" not in data:
240	        data["from_step"] = data.pop("from")
241	    if "python" in data and "python_exec" not in data:
242	        data["python_exec"] = data.pop("python")
243	    if "assets" in data and "asset" not in data:
244	        data["asset"] = data.pop("assets")
245	    return data

248	def parse_asset_entry(raw: str) -> tuple[str, Path | str]:
249	    if "=" not in raw:
250	        usage_error(f"artagents: invalid --asset value {raw!r}; expected KEY=PATH")
251	    key, path_text = raw.split("=", 1)
252	    key = key.strip()
253	    path_text = path_text.strip()
254	    if not key or not path_text:
255	        usage_error(f"artagents: invalid --asset value {raw!r}; expected KEY=PATH")
256	    if key == "main":
257	        usage_error("artagents: asset key 'main' is reserved; pass the primary video via --video")

462	def _coerce_frontmatter_value(raw: str) -> object:
463	    """Coerce a YAML-like scalar string into a Python value.
464	
465	    Recognizes: ``true``/``false`` (case-insensitive) -> bool; bare integers and
466	    floats -> numeric; strings wrapped in matching single or double quotes ->
467	    unquoted str; everything else -> raw str (whitespace-trimmed).
468	    """
469	    text = raw.strip()
470	    if not text:
471	        return ""
472	    lowered = text.lower()
473	    if lowered == "true":
474	        return True
475	    if lowered == "false":
476	        return False
477	    if (text.startswith("\"") and text.endswith("\"") and len(text) >= 2) or (
478	        text.startswith("'") and text.endswith("'") and len(text) >= 2
479	    ):
480	        return text[1:-1]
481	    try:
482	        return int(text)
483	    except ValueError:
484	        pass
485	    try:
486	        return float(text)
487	    except ValueError:
488	        pass
489	    return text
490	
491	
492	def parse_brief_frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[dict[str, object], str]:
493	    """Split an optional YAML-like ``---``-fenced frontmatter block off a brief.
494	
495	    The frontmatter must begin on line 1 with a line containing only ``---``,
496	    end with another line containing only ``---``, and contain
497	    ``key: value`` pairs (one per line). Blank lines and ``#`` comment lines
498	    inside the block are tolerated. When no frontmatter is present, returns
499	    ``({}, text)`` unchanged.
```

Perfect! Now I have enough information. Let me create a comprehensive summary:

## Summary

Based on my exploration of the ArtAgents codebase, here's how projects and timelines relate:

### 1. **Creating a Project (No Explicit "Project New" CLI)**
There is **no `artagents project new` command**. Instead, projects are created implicitly by specifying an `--out` directory when running an orchestrator. For example:
```bash
python3 -m artagents orchestrators run builtin.hype -- \
  --video source.mp4 \
  --brief brief.txt \
  --out /path/to/project_name \
  --render
```
The `--out` parameter **defines the project root** and is created on-demand (line 1019 in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/ArtAgents/artagents/executors/cut/run.py`):
```python
out_dir = args.out.resolve()
out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

### 2. **Project Directory Layout**
At the project level (`args.out`), storage includes:
- **`pool.json`** — Shared asset pool of media clips/sources (per-source level)
- **`scenes.json`**, **`transcript.json`**, **`shots.json`**, **`quality_zones.json`** — Video analysis outputs
- **`briefs/`** — Subdirectory containing brief-specific working directories

Each brief creates a subdirectory at `<out>/briefs/<brief_slug>/`, where `brief_slug` defaults to the brief filename stem (line 369 in hype/run.py):
```python
args.brief_out = (args.out / "briefs" / args.brief_slug).resolve()
```

### 3. **Timeline Creation (Orchestrator → Executor Pattern)**
`timeline.json` is **not created by CLI; it's written by the `cut` executor** during the arrange → cut pipeline. Timeline creation is implicit—there's no separate "create timeline" step. The flow is:

1. **Arrange executor** writes `arrangement.json` to `<out>/briefs/<brief_slug>/arrangement.json`
2. **Cut executor** reads the arrangement and writes three files to the same brief directory:
   - `hype.timeline.json` (line 1021 in cut/run.py)
   - `hype.assets.json` (line 1022)
   - `hype.metadata.json` (line 1023)

### 4. **Broad Storage at Project Level**
Living next to timeline at `<out>/briefs/<brief_slug>/`:
- **`arrangement.json`** — Arrangement data from arrange step
- **`hype.timeline.json`** — Timeline config (created by cut executor)
- **`hype.assets.json`** — Asset registry with file paths/URLs
- **`hype.metadata.json`** — Pipeline metadata (version, timestamps)
- **`refine.json`** — Editor refinements (optional, post-cut)
- **`brief.txt`** — Copy of the brief text
- **`editor_review.json`**, **`validation.json`** — Optional review/validation outputs

### 5. **Key File Paths**

| File | Created By | Path |
|------|------------|------|
| Project root | CLI (implicit) | `$OUT_DIR` |
| Pool | pool_build executor | `$OUT_DIR/pool.json` |
| Arrangement | arrange executor | `$OUT_DIR/briefs/$BRIEF_SLUG/arrangement.json` |
| Timeline | **cut executor** | `$OUT_DIR/briefs/$BRIEF_SLUG/hype.timeline.json` |
| Assets | **cut executor** | `$OUT_DIR/briefs/$BRIEF_SLUG/hype.assets.json` |
| Metadata | **cut executor** | `$OUT_DIR/briefs/$BRIEF_SLUG/hype.metadata.json` |

**Code snippet (timeline write location):**
```python
# artagents/executors/cut/run.py, lines 1021-1024
timeline_path_out = out_dir / "hype.timeline.json"
assets_path_out = out_dir / "hype.assets.json"
metadata_path_out = out_dir / "hype.metadata.json"
save_timeline(config, timeline_path_out)
```

```
23	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
24	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python3 -m artagents setup", description="Plan or apply ArtAgents local setup.")

51	        status = "applied" if apply else "planned"
52	        details = "; ".join(plan.command_lines())
53	        steps.append(SetupStep(name="elements install", status=status, detail=f"{element.kind}/{element.id}: {details}"))
54	    return tuple(steps)
55	
56	
57	def _plan_agents_symlink(root: Path, *, apply: bool) -> SetupStep:
58	    """Ensure AGENTS.md is a symlink to SKILL.md so both loaders read the same source."""
59	    agents = root / "AGENTS.md"
60	    target = "SKILL.md"
61	    skill = root / target
62	    if not skill.is_file():
63	        return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="warn", detail=f"{skill} missing; cannot link AGENTS.md")
64	    if agents.is_symlink() and (root / agents.readlink()).resolve() == skill.resolve():
65	        return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="ok", detail=f"AGENTS.md → {target}")
66	    if not agents.exists() and not agents.is_symlink():
67	        if apply:
68	            agents.symlink_to(target)
69	            return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="applied", detail=f"created AGENTS.md → {target}")
70	        return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="planned", detail=f"will create AGENTS.md → {target}")
71	    kind = "wrong symlink" if agents.is_symlink() else "regular file"
72	    if apply:
73	        agents.unlink()
74	        agents.symlink_to(target)
75	        return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="applied", detail=f"replaced AGENTS.md ({kind}) with symlink → {target}")
76	    return SetupStep(name="agents.md symlink", status="planned", detail=f"will replace AGENTS.md ({kind}) with symlink → {target}")
77	
78	
79	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
80	    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
81	    steps = plan_setup(apply=bool(args.apply))
82	    if args.json:
83	        payload = {
84	            "applied": bool(args.apply),
85	            "steps": [asdict(step) for step in steps],
86	        }
87	        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
88	        return 0
89	
90	    print("ArtAgents setup")
91	    if not args.apply:
92	        print("dry-run: pass --apply to sync managed defaults and run local element install commands")
93	    for step in steps:
94	        print(f"[{step.status}] {step.name}: {step.detail}")
95	    return 0
96	
97	
98	if __name__ == "__main__":
99	    raise SystemExit(main())
100
```

```
34	        description: str = "",

36	        outputs: tuple[ExecutorOutput | dict[str, Any], ...] | list[ExecutorOutput | dict[str, Any]] = (),

47	            "kind": kind,
48	            "version": version,
49	            "inputs": [_to_plain(input_) for input_ in inputs],
50	            "outputs": [_to_plain(output) for output in outputs],
```

IMPORTANT — LAUNCHER: bare `megaplan` is NOT on PATH on this system. Every megaplan CLI call you make MUST be invoked as `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan <args>`. Do not call bare `megaplan`.

## 1. Role & Mission
Your job is to drive the megaplan workflow through the CLI until the run finishes or a defined breakpoint requires the outer conversation.

Always follow these priorities, in order:
1. The latest user direction relayed through notes or resume messages.
2. The live CLI state from `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan status --plan <name>`.
3. The workflow and breakpoint rules in this template.
4. Your own memory of earlier turns.

Always do these things:
- Operate through the megaplan CLI only. Do not call workers or agents directly.
- Keep the outer conversation clean. Do not ask for routine confirmation.
- Use `next_step` and `valid_next` for routing. If memory and CLI state disagree, trust CLI state.
- Follow `orchestrator_guidance` after `gate` unless you have a concrete reason to disagree after checking plan artifacts or repository evidence yourself.
- Treat user notes as authoritative.

Never do these things:
- Do not run the workflow manually outside the CLI.
- Do not skip required phases for the selected robustness level.
- Do not emit a breakpoint unless one of the breakpoint rules below says to.

## 2. Startup
Start the run like this:
1. Run `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan init --project-dir [REDACTED] --robustness standard "<idea text above>"` (the auto-approve flag is omitted because raw_config.execution.auto_approve is explicitly true; the CLI honors the configured override).
2. Capture the returned plan name.
3. Output `PLAN_NAME: <name>` on its own line immediately after init and before any `BREAKPOINT:` or `COMPLETE:`.
4. Run `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan status --plan <name>`.
5. From then on, use that plan name for every command.

At startup and after every later resume:
- Read `state`, `next_step`, and `valid_next`.
- If `notes_count > 0`, read the full `notes` array before acting.
- Treat all notes as context. If the newest note changes direction, treat that note as the new intent.
- If `active_step` is present, treat it as an in-flight phase marker rather than a completed step. Use `last_step` for the most recent completed phase.

## 3. Phase Routing by Robustness
Standard robustness:
- `init -> prep -> plan -> critique -> gate`
- Then follow the gate decision tree below.
- `prep` may return `skip: true`; do not skip the command yourself.
- When you reach `gated`, run `finalize`.
- Then run `execute`.
- Then run `review`.
- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, the workflow becomes `finalized -> execute -> review` again until review passes or the CLI reaches its cap.

Gate decision tree:
- Condition 1: `gate_unset` — state is `critiqued` and `valid_next` includes `gate`. Action: run `gate`.
- Condition 2: `gate_iterate` — recommendation `ITERATE`, `valid_next` includes `revise`. Action: run `revise`, then continue back through `critique` and `gate`.
- Condition 3: `gate_escalate` — recommendation `ESCALATE`, `valid_next` offers override commands. Action: stop with `BREAKPOINT: GATE_ESCALATE`.
- Condition 4: `gate_proceed_blocked` — recommendation `PROCEED` but preflight blocked. Action: inspect `preflight_results` and revise; if unresolvable, stop with `BREAKPOINT: GATE_BLOCKED`.
- Condition 5: `gate_proceed` — recommendation `PROCEED` and preflight passed; state `gated`. Action: run `finalize`.

Review routing:
- If `review` succeeds, the run is done.
- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, run `execute` again, then `review` again. Capped at 3 cycles.

## 4. After Every Phase
After every phase command, immediately run:
`PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan status --plan <name>`

Then before choosing the next command:
- Re-read `state`, `next_step`, and `valid_next`.
- If `notes_count > 0`, read the full `notes` array.
- Check whether the newest note changes direction.
- If the last phase was `gate`, treat `orchestrator_guidance` as a literal routing hint.
- If response and `status` disagree, trust `status`.
- Prefer the explicit `valid_next` list over your own reconstruction.

## 5. Breakpoints
Format every breakpoint exactly:
`BREAKPOINT: <type>`
`Plan: <name>`
`State: <state>`
`Summary: <short reason>`
`Context: <artifacts, warnings, or the exact user decision needed>`

Types:
- `GATE_ESCALATE` — gate recommends ESCALATE.
- `GATE_BLOCKED` — gate_proceed_blocked unresolvable.
- `EXECUTE_APPROVAL` — finalize succeeded in review mode and execute needs approval. (Not applicable here — auto-approve.)
- `PHASE_ESCALATE` — non-execute phase still fails after the required retry.
- `EXECUTE_ESCALATE` — execute reaches the no-progress cap, or repeated blocking/timeouts.

## 6. Safeguards
Non-execute safeguards:
- If a non-execute phase fails or returns unusable output, retry that phase once with `--fresh`.
- If the same error appears twice for the same phase, the next retry must use `--fresh`.
- If still failing after the fresh retry, stop with `BREAKPOINT: PHASE_ESCALATE`.

Execute safeguards:
- Track forward progress per execute call. Forward progress = new completed tasks, completed batch, or state advance.
- 3 consecutive execute attempts without progress → `BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE`.

Review safeguards:
- `needs_rework` is normal; don't break out, follow the rework loop.
- Blocked review = review-phase problem, apply non-execute retry rule.

Notes / interruption:
- After any relaunch, run status and read all notes immediately. Treat the most recent note as the relaunch explanation.

## 7. Resume Protocol
On SendMessage resume:
1. Re-read the message.
2. Run status.
3. Read notes.
4. Resume from current state and `next_step`, not memory.

## 7A. Note Injection
- Use stored PLAN_NAME for note/status calls; if not captured, run `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan list` and use the most recent.
- Default to Option A (inject-at-boundary) unless the message clearly demands interruption.
- Option A: `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "<note>"`, confirm, no TaskStop.

## 8. Execution Details
Finalize and execute:
- After `gated`, run `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan finalize --plan <name>`.
- Auto-approve mode: run `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive`.

Per-batch execution:
- If the briefing or CLI response indicates per-batch, continue batch by batch.
- Use `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan progress --plan <name>` between batches.
- Re-run the same batch number after timeout if needed.

End conditions:
- Continue until `done`. Stop early only for a defined breakpoint.

## 9. Overrides & Plan Editing
- `add-note` safe from any active state.
- `force-proceed` from `critiqued` → `gated` (only with clear user intent).
- `force-proceed` cannot bypass missing project dir or success criteria.
- `replan` available from `critiqued`, `gated`, `finalized`. After replan, edit the plan file directly, then `critique`.
- `step add/remove/move` available in `planned`, `critiqued`, `gated`, `finalized`.

## 10. Completion Format
On completion, return exactly:
`COMPLETE: megaplan run finished`
`Plan: <name>`
`Final state: <state>`
`Summary: <outcome>`
`Artifacts: <key files or reports>`
`Follow-up: <only if something remains>`

## 11. Command Reference
All commands prefixed with `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan`:
- `status --plan <name>`
- `progress --plan <name>`
- `audit --plan <name>`
- `prep --plan <name>`
- `plan --plan <name>`
- `critique --plan <name>`
- `gate --plan <name>`
- `revise --plan <name>`
- `finalize --plan <name>`
- `execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive`
- `execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --batch N`
- `review --plan <name>`
- `override add-note --plan <name> --note "..."`
- `override force-proceed --plan <name> --reason "..."`
- `override replan --plan <name> --reason "..." [--note "..."]`
- `override abort --plan <name> --reason "..."`
- `step add --plan <name> --after S<N> "description"`
- `step remove --plan <name> S<N>`
- `step move --plan <name> S<N> --after S<M>`

## Startup
1. Run `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan status --plan add-a-project-projecttimeline-20260503-2303`.
2. Read `state`, `active_step`, `notes`. If active_step.step == "execute" and active_step.health == "healthy", DO NOT issue a duplicate execute — wait. Use the Bash tool with a sleep loop to poll status every ~5 minutes until active_step is gone OR active_step.health is "stale"/"unhealthy".
3. Once execute returns and a new state is reached, follow the routing rules below.

## Routing
- After each `execute --batch N` returns, run `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan progress --plan <name>` to confirm batch N is "done", then `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan status --plan <name>` to read state.
- If state == "finalized" and there are more batches pending, run `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --batch <N+1>`. Continue until all batches are done.
- When the final batch completes, the state will advance to "executed". Then run `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan review --plan <name>`.
- If review returns "needs_rework", the state goes back to "finalized" with next_step "execute". Re-run execute (per-batch as needed), then review again. Capped at 3 rework cycles by the CLI.
- If review returns success, the run is done.

## Safeguards
- Track forward progress per execute call. Forward progress = a batch transitioning to done, or state advancing to "executed".
- 3 consecutive execute attempts without forward progress → stop with `BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE`.
- Non-execute phase fails twice in a row → retry with `--fresh`. Still fails → `BREAKPOINT: PHASE_ESCALATE`.

## Polling the active step
While an execute is running on the codex side, poll like this:
```
PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m megaplan status --plan add-a-project-projecttimeline-20260503-2303
```

But terminate the loop when you see "DONE" so you can act.

Better: just call status, branch, sleep with `Bash` tool's run_in_background or a brief synchronous sleep (270s max to stay under cache), and re-call.

## Context

Megaplan source: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan` (a separate repo from the one I'm currently working in). User-config is at `~/.config/megaplan/config.json`. Profiles already exist as a concept — see `megaplan config profiles list` / `megaplan config profiles show <name>`. The built-in profile definitions live in `megaplan/profiles/*.toml`. Profiles are resolved built-in → user → project per `~/.config/megaplan/profiles.toml` and `<project>/.megaplan/profiles.toml`. The `--profile <name>` flag already works at `init` time; this task is about persisting a profile choice as the *config default*.

The current state I observed: there is no `agents.profile` virtual key. Setting `agents.profile <name>` errors with `Unknown step 'profile'. Valid steps: plan, prep, critique, ...`. Today the user has to run `config set agents.<phase> <value>` once per phase (12 times) to apply a profile.

**Repo state when I last checked:** branch `megaplan/per-milestone-robustness-20260503`, uncommitted changes already in `cloud.yaml` and `megaplan/cli.py`. **Do not touch those uncommitted changes** — diff first, work only in additive ways, and leave them intact for the user. Stay on the current branch — do not switch or create a new one.

## What to build

Pick the cleaner of these two designs (your call, but explain in your final report which you chose and why):

**Option A** — Add a new subcommand: `megaplan config use-profile <name>` that loads the named profile (using the existing profile resolution chain) and writes all phase keys into the user config file at once. This is most aligned with how `config profiles list/show` are already structured.

**Option B** — Make `config set agents.profile <name>` a virtual shortcut that does the same thing.

Either way, the result must be that running it leaves `~/.config/megaplan/config.json` with `agents.<phase>` populated for every phase from the named profile, identical to what `config profiles show <name>` would print.

Requirements:
- Must support all built-in profiles (`standard`, `all-codex`, `all-deepseek-flash`, `all-open`, etc.) plus any user/project-defined profiles.
- Must error with a clear message if the profile name is unknown.
- Must NOT clobber unrelated config keys (like `execution.auto_approve`).
- Existing per-phase `config set agents.<phase> <agent>` must keep working unchanged.
- If there's a tests/ directory with config tests, add a small test for the new behavior. If the test framework requires a fixture for the user config path, mock or use a temp dir — don't write into the real `~/.config/megaplan/config.json` from a test.
- Don't commit. Leave the changes staged or unstaged for the user to review.

```
143	def apply_profile_expansion(
144	    args: argparse.Namespace,
145	    project_dir: Path | None,
146	    state: dict | None = None,
147	) -> argparse.Namespace:
148	    if getattr(args, "_profile_applied", False):
149	        return args
150	
151	    profile_name = getattr(args, "profile", None)
152	    if profile_name is None and state is not None:
153	        profile_name = (state.get("config") or {}).get("profile")
154	    phase_models = list(getattr(args, "phase_model", None) or [])
155	
156	    if profile_name:
157	        profiles = load_profiles(project_dir=project_dir)
158	        resolved = resolve_profile(profile_name, profiles)
159	        phase_models.extend(profile_to_phase_models(resolved))
160	        args.profile = profile_name
161	
162	    # Merge persisted --phase-model overrides from plan state. CLI flags on the
163	    # current step invocation take precedence; persisted values fill in gaps for
164	    # steps not specified on the CLI.
165	    if state is not None:
166	        persisted = list((state.get("config") or {}).get("phase_model") or [])
167	        cli_steps = {pm.split("=", 1)[0] for pm in phase_models if "=" in pm}
168	        for pm in persisted:
169	            if "=" in pm and pm.split("=", 1)[0] not in cli_steps:
170	                phase_models.append(pm)
171	
172	    args.phase_model = phase_models
173	    args._profile_applied = True
174	    return args
```

For the test, I'll use `monkeypatch.setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ...)` to redirect the real config_dir without touching home. Now I'll design the implementation.

**Decision: Option A** (`config use-profile <name>`). Reasoning: a profile is conceptually different from a single-key set (it writes 12 keys at once, and deals with agent specs containing `:` like `hermes:glm-5.1` that don't validate cleanly through the existing `agents.<phase>` path which checks `value not in KNOWN_AGENTS`). A new subcommand sits cleanly alongside `config profiles list/show`.

Note there's a real bug here worth flagging: `config set agents.<phase>` rejects values like `hermes:glm-5.1` because it checks `value not in KNOWN_AGENTS`, but profiles use those specs freely. We need to bypass that check when applying a profile. I'll do the writes directly.

## Report

**Option chosen: A** — added `megaplan config use-profile <name>`. Reasons: (1) it sits naturally alongside the existing `config profiles list/show` family; (2) the existing `config set agents.<phase>` validator rejects values containing `:` because it checks `value not in KNOWN_AGENTS`, but profiles routinely use specs like `hermes:glm-5.1`. Overloading `agents.profile` would have meant either weakening that validator or carving an awkward virtual-key special case. A new subcommand bypasses that mess cleanly.

**Files changed (uncommitted, on branch `megaplan/per-milestone-robustness-20260503`):**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/megaplan/cli.py`
  - lines ~903-930: new `action == "use-profile"` branch in `handle_config`
  - lines ~1049-1060: new `use-profile` argparse subparser under `config_sub`
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/tests/test_config.py`
  - imports updated (added `profiles_module`, `CliError`, `DEFAULT_AGENT_ROUTING`)
  - lines ~278-352: two new tests

**CLI invocation that now works:** `megaplan config use-profile standard` (also `all-codex`, `all-deepseek-flash`, `all-open`, any user/project profile, etc.). Verified manually: writes 12 `agents.<phase>` keys, preserves `execution.auto_approve` and other unrelated keys, exits 1 with `unknown_profile` on a bad name, and the resulting `agents` block matches `config profiles show <name>` exactly.

**Tests added:** two in `tests/test_config.py` — `test_handle_config_use_profile_writes_all_phase_keys_and_preserves_unrelated` (success path + preservation + parity with `profiles show`) and `test_handle_config_use_profile_unknown_profile_raises`. Both use the existing `isolated_config_dir` fixture and additionally monkey-patch `profiles_module.config_dir` so the user-layer `profiles.toml` lookup is also redirected. Both pass. The pre-existing `test_build_parser_init_flags_are_tristate` failure is unrelated (PyYAML missing on the test interpreter).

**Worth flagging, not fixed:**
1. `config set agents.<phase> hermes:glm-5.1` currently errors with `Unknown agent 'hermes:glm-5.1'` because the validator at cli.py:831 compares the raw spec against `KNOWN_AGENTS` instead of `parse_agent_spec(value)[0]`. Profiles work around this; manual `config set` for a hermes-with-model phase does not. This is the underlying reason the new shortcut is more than just sugar.
2. `Unknown profile` lists profile names alphabetically without source labels, so a user with a project-layer profile shadowing a built-in can't tell from the error which layer wins. Minor.

```
292	def _infer_source_kind(asset: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
293	    asset_type = asset.get("type")
294	    if isinstance(asset_type, str):
295	        if asset_type.startswith("video/"):
296	            return "video"
297	        if asset_type.startswith("audio/"):
298	            return "audio"
299	        if asset_type.startswith("image/"):
300	            return "image"
301	    return "other"

304	def _normalize_asset(raw: Any, *, path: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
305	    data = _require_mapping(raw, path)
306	    has_file = isinstance(data.get("file"), str) and bool(data.get("file"))
307	    has_url = isinstance(data.get("url"), str) and bool(data.get("url"))
308	    if has_file == has_url:
309	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path} must contain exactly one of file or url")
310	    payload = dict(data)
311	    if has_file:
312	        payload["file"] = str(Path(payload["file"]).expanduser().resolve())
313	        payload.pop("url", None)
314	    else:
315	        payload["url"] = payload["url"]
316	        payload.pop("file", None)
317	    return payload
```

```
3	import type { TimelineAction } from '@/tools/video-editor/types/timeline-canvas';
4	
5	export const DURATION_KEYS = ['speed', 'from', 'to', 'hold'] as const;
6	
7	export function patchAffectsDuration(patch: Partial<ClipMeta>): boolean {
8	  return DURATION_KEYS.some((key) => key in patch);
9	}
10	
11	export function recalcActionEnd(action: TimelineAction, merged: Partial<ClipMeta>): number {
12	  const speed = merged.speed ?? 1;
13	  const fallbackSourceDuration = Math.max(0, (action.end - action.start) * speed);
14	  const sourceDuration = typeof merged.hold === 'number'
15	    ? merged.hold
16	    : Math.max(
17	      0,
18	      (merged.to ?? fallbackSourceDuration + (merged.from ?? 0)) - (merged.from ?? 0),
19	    );
20	
21	  return action.start + sourceDuration / speed;
22	}
23	
24	export function splitIntersectingClipsAtPlayhead(
25	  resolvedConfig: NonNullable<TimelineData['resolvedConfig']>,
26	  rows: TimelineData['rows'],
27	  clipIds: string[],
28	  currentTime: number,
29	): {
30	  config: NonNullable<TimelineData['resolvedConfig']>;
31	  didSplit: boolean;
32	} {
33	  const intersectingClipIds = new Set<string>();
34	
35	  for (const row of rows) {
36	    for (const action of row.actions) {
37	      if (
38	        clipIds.includes(action.id)
39	        && action.start <= currentTime
40	        && currentTime < action.end
41	      ) {
42	        intersectingClipIds.add(action.id);
43	      }
44	    }
45	  }
46	
47	  if (intersectingClipIds.size === 0) {
48	    return { config: resolvedConfig, didSplit: false };
49	  }
50	
51	  let nextResolvedConfig = resolvedConfig;
52	  let didSplit = false;
53	
54	  for (const clipId of clipIds) {
55	    if (!intersectingClipIds.has(clipId)) {
56	      continue;
57	    }
58	
59	    const splitResult = splitClipAtPlayhead(nextResolvedConfig, clipId, currentTime);
60	    if (!splitResult.nextSelectedClipId) {
61	      continue;
62	    }
63	
64	    nextResolvedConfig = splitResult.config;
65	    didSplit = true;
66	  }
67	
68	  return {
69	    config: nextResolvedConfig,
70	    didSplit,
71	  };
72	}
```

## Capability Comparison: ArtAgents Timeline vs reigh-app Editor

### 1. **Side-by-Side Feature Matrix**

| Capability | reigh-app Editor | ArtAgents Timeline | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Clip Position** | First-class: `at` (timeline start) | First-class: `at` | Both identical |
| **Clip Duration (from source)** | First-class: `from`, `to`, `speed` | First-class: `from`, `to`, `speed` | Both identical |
| **Clip Hold (synthetic duration)** | First-class: `hold` | First-class: `hold` | Both identical |
| **Speed Control** | 0.1–4.0x scrubber in UI, stored as `speed` | Opaque in `params`; no first-class support | AA has no typed speed—must live in params if needed |
| **Opacity** | First-class: `opacity` slider (0–1) | First-class: `opacity` | Both identical |
| **Volume** | First-class: `volume` slider (0–1) | First-class: `volume` | Both identical |
| **Audio Mute** | Track-level `muted` bool | Track-level `muted` bool | Both at track level; clip-level mute not exposed in AA |
| **Position (X, Y)** | First-class: `x`, `y` (pixels) | First-class: `x`, `y` | Both identical |
| **Dimensions (W, H)** | First-class: `width`, `height` | First-class: `width`, `height` | Both identical |
| **Cropping** | First-class: `cropTop`, `cropBottom`, `cropLeft`, `cropRight` | First-class: same fields | Both identical |
| **Entrance Animation** | Typed: `entrance` {type, duration, intensity?, params?} | Typed: `entrance` (same) | Both identical |
| **Exit Animation** | Typed: `exit` {type, duration, intensity?, params?} | Typed: `exit` (same) | Both identical |
| **Continuous Effect** | Typed: `continuous` {type, intensity?, params?} | Typed: `continuous` (same) | Both identical |
| **Transition** | Typed: `transition` {type, duration} | Typed: `transition` (same) | Both identical |
| **Text Clip** | First-class: `text` {content, fontFamily, fontSize, color, align, bold, italic} | First-class: `text` (same) | Both identical |
| **Blend Mode** | Track-level `blendMode` (normal, multiply, screen, overlay, etc.) | Track-level `blendMode` (same) | Both at track level; clip-level not typed in either |
| **Effects List** | `effects` field (fade_in, fade_out) | `effects` field (opaque list) | AA allows arbitrary effects list but no type spec |
| **Parameters** | `params` (opaque dict for effect config) | `params` (opaque dict) | Both identical |
| **Generation Metadata** | `generation` (opaque dict for provenance) | `generation` (opaque dict) | Both identical |
| **Pool/Arrangement Metadata** | None | `pool_id`, `clip_order`, `source_uuid` | AA-only fields for upstream production tracking |
| **Clip Type** | `clipType` string; built-in: media, hold, text, effect-layer | `clipType` string; same built-ins | Both open strings at schema level |
| **Audio Reactive** | Editor detects via effect code & parameters | No first-class support | AA would need custom effect handling |
| **Reverse/Playback** | Not in current schema | Not in current schema | Neither editor supports video reversal |
| **Keyframes** | Not in current schema | Not in current schema | Neither supports animated parameter curves |
| **Markers/Cue Points** | Not in current schema | Not in current schema | Neither supports timeline markers |
| **Masks** | Not in current schema | Not in current schema | Neither supports clip masking |
| **Color Correction** | Not in current schema | Not in current schema | Would live in opaque `params` |
| **Track Organization** | Flat list; visual + audio | Flat list; visual + audio | Both identical |
| **Track Properties** | id, kind, label, scale, fit, opacity, volume, muted, blendMode | id, kind, label, scale, fit, opacity, volume, muted, blendMode | Both identical |
| **Theme System** | `theme` slug + `theme_overrides` dict | `theme` slug + `theme_overrides` dict | Both identical |
| **Generation Defaults** | `generation_defaults` opaque dict | `generation_defaults` opaque dict | Both identical |
| **Pinned Shot Groups** | `pinnedShotGroups` array (Banodoco-only) | `pinnedShotGroups` array | Both identical |

### 2. **First-Class vs Opaque Fields**

**reigh-app Editor (all first-class typed in TimelineClip):**
- Position, dimensions, crops: x, y, width, height, cropTop/Bottom/Left/Right
- Timing/speed: at, from, to, speed, hold
- Audio: volume
- Opacity
- Text rendering: text object (content, fontFamily, fontSize, color, align, bold, italic)
- Animations: entrance, exit, continuous (typed objects with duration, intensity, params)
- Transition: typed object
- Asset reference: asset (string ID)
- Track assignment: track, clipType
- Provenance: source_uuid, generation, pool_id, clip_order

**ArtAgents (all fields match reigh-app exactly)**
- Same first-class typed fields as above
- Both use banodoco-timeline-schema as the shared schema source

**Both use opaque `params` dict for:**
- Effect-specific configuration
- Effect parameter values (numbers, booleans, color strings, audio-reactive bindings)
- Sequence metadata (for effect-layer clips)

---

### 3. **Structural Convergence Assessment**

**Are they converged?** Nearly yes, with caveats.

**Why they converge:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts` explicitly imports from `@banodoco/timeline-schema`:
  ```typescript
  export type {
    TimelineConfigT as SharedTimelineConfig,
    TimelineClipT as SharedTimelineClip,
    ...
  } from '@banodoco/timeline-schema';
  ```
- ArtAgents `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/ArtAgents/artagents/timeline.py` re-exports the same Zod schema via `banodoco_timeline_schema`
- Both materialize to `TimelineConfig` + `AssetRegistry` types (defined in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/banodoco-workspace/packages/timeline-schema/typescript/src/schemas.ts`)

**Structural differences:**
- **reigh-app** maintains richer **in-editor** shapes (`ResolvedTimelineConfig`, `ClipMeta`, `ClipOrderMap`) for UI state but persists only the shared schema
- **ArtAgents** works directly with the shared schema + additional Banodoco production fields (`pool_id`, `clip_order`, `source_uuid`) that are carry-forward-only (not generated by AA)
- Both support **flat track lists** (no nesting, no grouped compositions at the schema level)

**Can they converge further?**
- Yes. They already share schema. AA could adopt reigh-app's in-memory `ClipMeta` + `ClipOrderMap` helpers if doing rich edits.
- Both would benefit from a shared schema validation library (currently Zod in TS, loose validation in Python).

---

### 4. **Top 5 Gaps to Close in ArtAgents**

1. **Speed control as first-class field** (`speed` typed but editor UI supports 0.1–4.0x scrubber)
   - Currently opaque in `params`; should surface as `speed: float` (already in schema, just needs UI scaffolding)
   - Impact: Medium (speed is heavily used in reigh-app, AA may not expose it yet)

2. **Clip-level audio mute** (currently only track-level `muted`)
   - reigh-app has track-level; AA should add `muted?: bool` to `TimelineClip`
   - Impact: Low-Medium (workaround: mute entire track or silence in opaque params)

3. **Audio reactivity first-class support** (currently embedded in effect code strings)
   - reigh-app editor detects audio-reactive effects via code introspection + parameter type hints (`audio-binding`)
   - AA should add schema hints to `ParameterDefinition` or effect metadata
   - Impact: Medium (AA agents need to know which effects react to audio for prompt generation)

4. **Keyframes / parameter animation** (completely absent in both)
   - Current gap: neither supports animated parameter curves (opacity fade, speed ramp, etc.)
   - AA could add `keyframes: Array<{at: number, params: dict}>` to clip
   - Impact: High (limits dynamic effects; both need this for professional output)

5. **Markers / timeline cues** (absent in both)
   - No support for user-placed markers, section labels, or beat-sync points
   - AA could add `markers: Array<{at: number, label: string, color?: string}>`
   - Impact: Low-Medium (nice-to-have for agent reasoning about pacing/structure)

---

### 5. **Things NOT to Copy from reigh-app**

- **In-memory `ClipOrderMap`** (computed from clips, not persisted): AA doesn't need this unless doing rich UI editing
- **`ResolvedTimelineConfig` shape** (asset registry merged with config): AA can keep these separate; resolve at render time
- **`PinnedShotGroup` arrays** (Banodoco-only, for UI grouping): AA should keep this but note it's not portable across tools
- **No need to copy:** reigh-app's Remotion/React rendering layer—AA is Python/CLI and will use its own renderer
- **Deprecated patterns:** reigh-app has migrated away from `effects` as `Record<string, number>` to an array; avoid the old dict form in AA

I want a rigorous design analysis — not an implementation plan, but a deep architectural critique — of one specific proposal for the ArtAgents project-timeline schema, with alternatives considered.

## Context

We just shipped a new "project timeline" abstraction in ArtAgents (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/ArtAgents/artagents/core/project/`). It's a *placement / composition layer* that sits ABOVE the existing Banodoco timeline schema (the renderable TimelineConfig + TimelineClip + AssetRegistry).

**The two layers, concretely:**

1. **Placement (new, upstream authoring layer):**
   - File: `artagents/core/project/schema.py` (`build_placement`, `validate_placement`, lines 111–149, 249–271)
   - Typed fields: `id`, `track`, `at`, `from`, `to`, `source` (a ref — either a project source or a run-clip), `entrance`, `exit`, `transition`, `effects` (opaque list), `params` (opaque dict)
   - Stored in `<project>/timeline.json`

2. **Materialized TimelineClip (existing, downstream renderable layer):**
   - Defined in `@banodoco/timeline-schema` (TS Zod), surfaced in Python via `artagents/timeline.py` and the `banodoco_timeline_schema` package.
   - First-class fields on a clip: `at`, `from`, `to`, `speed`, `hold`, `opacity`, `volume`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `cropTop/Bottom/Left/Right`, `text` object, `entrance`, `exit`, `continuous`, `transition`, `clipType`, `asset`, plus production-tracking carries (`source_uuid`, `pool_id`, `clip_order`, `generation`).
   - This is what reigh-app's editor writes/reads directly.

**Materialization** happens in `artagents/core/project/materialize.py` (lines 1–~100). It walks placements, resolves source/run-clip refs against `AssetRegistry`, and produces a flat `TimelineConfig` + `AssetRegistry`. Today, almost no per-clip visual properties can be expressed at the placement layer — they have to be added later on the materialized clip, or stuffed into opaque `params`.

**Key constraint:** the Banodoco timeline schema is shared with reigh-app and must NOT be modified from the AA side. We can extend the placement schema freely.

**Tension we've identified:**
- The placement layer's value is composition (referencing run-clips, building timelines from agent runs). It is NOT a pixel-level editor.
- But users probably will want to set things like `speed`, `opacity`, `x/y/width/height`, `text`, `entrance/exit/transition` from the placement layer too, since those ARE authoring decisions, not render-time decisions.
- We could either: (a) embed all those fields directly into placement; (b) add an optional `clip_overrides` field whose shape mirrors Banodoco's TimelineClip (minus identity); (c) keep placements minimal and require a separate "edit pass" on materialized output; (d) something else.

## The proposal to critique

> Option 3a: keep placement minimal AND add an optional `clip_overrides` field whose shape is exactly Banodoco's `TimelineClip` (minus identity fields like id/asset/track/clipType, which the placement already determines). At materialize time, the resolved clip = base-clip-from-source merged with `clip_overrides`. That gives reigh-app's editing power when wanted, without bloating placement or duplicating the Banodoco model.

## What I want back

A deep critique under ~700 words. Concretely:

1. **Tradeoffs of the proposal.** What does coupling the placement schema to TimelineClip's shape buy us, and what does it cost us? Be specific about coupling: if Banodoco's schema evolves, what breaks here? If a placement's source is a run-clip that was generated with its OWN clip-shaped properties (because reigh-app authored it), how do `clip_overrides` interact — do they layer on top, replace, conflict?

2. **The merge semantics question.** "Resolved clip = base merged with overrides" is hand-wavy. Spell out the actual merge: which fields override scalar (replace), which deep-merge (e.g. `entrance`), which append (`effects`), which conflict in non-obvious ways. Identify cases where the merge is genuinely ambiguous.

3. **Re-materialization and edit survival.** The user edits a placement's `clip_overrides`. Then a downstream run regenerates the source run-clip. Re-materialize: do user edits survive? Should they? What if the source's *own* baked-in properties changed in ways the override now contradicts?

4. **Alternatives worth considering** (briefly):
   - (a) Embed clip fields directly into placement (no nesting).
   - (c) Keep placement minimal, edit only on materialized output, accept that materialized timelines are user-edited downstream and never re-materialized in place.
   - (d) Two-layer placement: composition placement + optional render placement, where render placements are the TimelineClip-shaped overrides.

```
183	        if normalized["id"] in seen:
184	            raise ProjectValidationError(f"duplicate placement id: {normalized['id']}")
185	        seen.add(normalized["id"])
186	        normalized_placements.append(normalized)
187	    tracks = data.get("tracks", [])
188	    if not isinstance(tracks, list):
189	        raise ProjectValidationError("timeline.tracks must be a list")
190	    payload = dict(data)
191	    payload.update(
192	        {
193	            "placements": normalized_placements,
194	            "project_slug": project_slug,
195	            "schema_version": TIMELINE_SCHEMA_VERSION,
196	            "tracks": deepcopy(tracks),
197	        }
198	    )
199	    payload.setdefault("created_at", utc_now_iso())
200	    payload.setdefault("updated_at", payload["created_at"])
201	    return payload

204	def validate_source(raw: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
205	    data = _require_mapping(raw, "source")
206	    _require_version(data, SOURCE_SCHEMA_VERSION, "source")
207	    payload = dict(data)
208	    payload.update(
209	        {
210	            "asset": _normalize_asset(data.get("asset"), path="source.asset"),
211	            "kind": validate_source_kind(data.get("kind"), path="source.kind"),
212	            "metadata": _optional_mapping(data.get("metadata", {}), "source.metadata"),
213	            "project_slug": validate_project_slug(_require_string(data.get("project_slug"), "source.project_slug")),
214	            "schema_version": SOURCE_SCHEMA_VERSION,
215	            "source_id": validate_source_id(_require_string(data.get("source_id"), "source.source_id")),
216	        }
217	    )
218	    payload.setdefault("created_at", utc_now_iso())
219	    payload.setdefault("updated_at", payload["created_at"])
220	    return payload

222	
223	def validate_run_record(raw: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
224	    data = _require_mapping(raw, "run")
225	    _require_version(data, RUN_SCHEMA_VERSION, "run")
226	    status = _require_string(data.get("status"), "run.status")
227	    if status not in RUN_STATUSES:
228	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"run.status must be one of {sorted(RUN_STATUSES)}")
229	    payload = dict(data)
230	    payload.update(
231	        {
232	            "artifacts": _optional_mapping(data.get("artifacts", {}), "run.artifacts"),
233	            "metadata": _optional_mapping(data.get("metadata", {}), "run.metadata"),
234	            "project_slug": validate_project_slug(_require_string(data.get("project_slug"), "run.project_slug")),
235	            "run_id": validate_run_id(_require_string(data.get("run_id"), "run.run_id")),
236	            "schema_version": RUN_SCHEMA_VERSION,
237	            "status": status,
238	        }
239	    )
240	    if "argv" in payload:
241	        argv = payload["argv"]
242	        if not isinstance(argv, list) or not all(isinstance(item, str) for item in argv):
243	            raise ProjectValidationError("run.argv must be a list of strings")
244	    payload.setdefault("created_at", utc_now_iso())
245	    payload.setdefault("updated_at", payload["created_at"])
246	    return payload

248	
249	def validate_placement(raw: Any, *, path: str = "placement") -> dict[str, Any]:
250	    data = _require_mapping(raw, path)
251	    payload = dict(data)
252	    payload["id"] = validate_placement_id(_require_string(data.get("id"), f"{path}.id"))
253	    payload["track"] = _require_string(data.get("track"), f"{path}.track")
254	    payload["at"] = _require_number(data.get("at"), f"{path}.at")
255	    if payload["at"] < 0:
256	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path}.at must be greater than or equal to 0")
257	    payload["source"] = validate_reference(data.get("source"), path=f"{path}.source")
258	    if "from" in payload:
259	        payload["from"] = _require_number(payload["from"], f"{path}.from")
260	        if payload["from"] < 0:
261	            raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path}.from must be greater than or equal to 0")
262	    if "to" in payload:
263	        payload["to"] = _require_number(payload["to"], f"{path}.to")
264	        trim_from = payload.get("from", 0)
265	        if payload["to"] <= trim_from:
266	            raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path}.to must be greater than {path}.from")
267	    if "effects" in payload and not isinstance(payload["effects"], list):
268	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path}.effects must be a list")
269	    if "params" in payload and not isinstance(payload["params"], dict):
270	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path}.params must be an object")
271	    return payload
272	
273	
274	def validate_reference(raw: Any, *, path: str = "source") -> dict[str, Any]:
275	    data = _require_mapping(raw, path)
276	    kind = _require_string(data.get("kind"), f"{path}.kind")
277	    if kind not in REF_KINDS:
278	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path}.kind must be one of {sorted(REF_KINDS)}")
279	    if kind == "source":
280	        return {"id": validate_source_id(_require_string(data.get("id"), f"{path}.id")), "kind": "source"}
281	    ref = {"clip_id": _require_string(data.get("clip_id"), f"{path}.clip_id"), "kind": "run", "run_id": validate_run_id(data.get("run_id"))}
282	    return ref
283	
284	
285	def validate_source_kind(raw: Any, *, path: str = "source.kind") -> str:
286	    kind = _require_string(raw, path)
287	    if kind not in SOURCE_KINDS:
288	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path} must be one of {sorted(SOURCE_KINDS)}")
289	    return kind
290	
291	
292	def _infer_source_kind(asset: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
293	    asset_type = asset.get("type")
294	    if isinstance(asset_type, str):
295	        if asset_type.startswith("video/"):
296	            return "video"
297	        if asset_type.startswith("audio/"):
298	            return "audio"
299	        if asset_type.startswith("image/"):
300	            return "image"
301	    return "other"
302	
303	
304	def _normalize_asset(raw: Any, *, path: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
305	    data = _require_mapping(raw, path)
306	    has_file = isinstance(data.get("file"), str) and bool(data.get("file"))
307	    has_url = isinstance(data.get("url"), str) and bool(data.get("url"))
308	    if has_file == has_url:
309	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path} must contain exactly one of file or url")
310	    payload = dict(data)
311	    if has_file:
312	        payload["file"] = str(Path(payload["file"]).expanduser().resolve())
313	        payload.pop("url", None)
314	    else:
315	        payload["url"] = payload["url"]
316	        payload.pop("file", None)
317	    return payload
318	
319	
320	def _require_version(data: dict[str, Any], expected: int, path: str) -> None:
321	    if data.get("schema_version") != expected:
322	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path}.schema_version must be {expected}")
323	
324	
325	def _require_mapping(raw: Any, path: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
326	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
327	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path} must be an object")
328	    return raw
329	
330	
331	def _optional_mapping(raw: Any, path: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
332	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
333	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path} must be an object")
334	    return dict(raw)
335	
336	
337	def _require_string(raw: Any, path: str) -> str:
338	    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw:
339	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path} must be a non-empty string")
340	    return raw
341	
342	
343	def _require_number(raw: Any, path: str) -> int | float:
344	    if not isinstance(raw, (int, float)) or isinstance(raw, bool):
345	        raise ProjectValidationError(f"{path} must be a number")
346	    return raw
```

```
1	"""Materialize ArtAgents project timelines into renderable timeline files."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from copy import deepcopy
6	from pathlib import Path

21	class ProjectMaterializeError(RuntimeError):
22	    """Raised when a project timeline cannot be materialized."""

25	def materialize_project_timeline(
26	    project_slug: str,
27	    *,
28	    root: str | Path | None = None,
29	    theme: str = DEFAULT_THEME,
30	) -> tuple[banodoco_timeline.TimelineConfig, banodoco_timeline.AssetRegistry]:
31	    require_project(project_slug, root=root)
32	    project_timeline = load_timeline(project_slug, root=root)
33	    return materialize_project_timeline_payload(project_timeline, root=root, theme=theme)

36	def materialize_project_timeline_payload(
37	    project_timeline: dict[str, Any],
38	    *,
39	    root: str | Path | None = None,
40	    theme: str = DEFAULT_THEME,
41	) -> tuple[banodoco_timeline.TimelineConfig, banodoco_timeline.AssetRegistry]:
42	    project_timeline = validate_project_timeline(project_timeline)
43	    project_slug = project_timeline["project_slug"]
44	    clips: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
45	    registry: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
46	
47	    for placement in project_timeline.get("placements", []):
48	        ref = placement.get("source", {})
49	        if ref.get("kind") == "source":
50	            source_id = ref["id"]
51	            source = require_source(project_slug, source_id, root=root)
52	            asset_key = f"source:{source_id}"
53	            registry[asset_key] = deepcopy(source["asset"])
54	            clips.append(_clip_from_source_placement(placement, asset_key=asset_key))
55	            continue
56	        if ref.get("kind") == "run":
57	            clip, run_registry = require_run_clip(project_slug, ref["run_id"], ref["clip_id"], root=root)
58	            materialized_clip = _clip_from_run_placement(
59	                placement,
60	                clip,
61	                project_slug=project_slug,
62	                run_id=ref["run_id"],
63	                registry=registry,
64	                run_registry=run_registry,
65	                root=root,
66	            )
67	            clips.append(materialized_clip)
68	            continue
69	        raise ProjectMaterializeError(f"placement {placement.get('id')!r} has unsupported source kind {ref.get('kind')!r}")
70	
71	    config: banodoco_timeline.TimelineConfig = {
72	        "theme": theme,
73	        "clips": clips,
74	    }
75	    tracks = project_timeline.get("tracks")
76	    if tracks:
77	        config["tracks"] = deepcopy(tracks)
78	    assets: banodoco_timeline.AssetRegistry = {"assets": registry}
79	    banodoco_timeline.validate_timeline(config)
80	    banodoco_timeline.validate_registry(assets)
81	    return config, assets
82

84	def require_run_clip(
85	    project_slug: str,
86	    run_id: str,
87	    clip_id: str,
88	    *,
89	    root: str | Path | None = None,
90	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], banodoco_timeline.AssetRegistry]:
91	    require_run_record(project_slug, run_id, root=root)
92	    timeline_path = paths.run_timeline_path(project_slug, run_id, root=root)
93	    assets_path = paths.run_assets_path(project_slug, run_id, root=root)
94	    if not timeline_path.is_file():
95	        raise FileNotFoundError(
96	            f"run timeline not found for {run_id}: {timeline_path}. "
97	            f"Next command: python3 -m artagents projects show --project {project_slug}"
98	        )
99	    if not assets_path.is_file():
100	        raise FileNotFoundError(
101	            f"run assets not found for {run_id}: {assets_path}. "
102	            f"Next command: rerun the tool with --project {project_slug} or inspect {timeline_path}"
103	        )
104	    run_timeline = banodoco_timeline.load_timeline(timeline_path)
105	    run_registry = banodoco_timeline.load_registry(assets_path)
106	    for clip in run_timeline.get("clips", []):
107	        if isinstance(clip, dict) and clip.get("id") == clip_id:
108	            return deepcopy(clip), run_registry
109	    available = sorted(
110	        str(clip.get("id"))
111	        for clip in run_timeline.get("clips", [])
112	        if isinstance(clip, dict) and isinstance(clip.get("id"), str)
113	    )
114	    detail = f" Available clip ids: {', '.join(available)}." if available else " The run timeline has no clip ids."
115	    raise FileNotFoundError(
116	        f"clip not found in run {run_id}: {clip_id}.{detail} "
117	        f"Next command: inspect {timeline_path} and pass --clip <clip-id>."
118	    )
119	
120	
121	def _clip_from_source_placement(placement: dict[str, Any], *, asset_key: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
122	    clip: dict[str, Any] = {
123	        "asset": asset_key,
124	        "at": placement["at"],
125	        "clipType": "media",
126	        "id": placement["id"],
127	        "track": placement["track"],
128	    }
129	    for source_key, clip_key in (("from", "from"), ("to", "to")):
130	        if source_key in placement:
131	            clip[clip_key] = placement[source_key]
132	    for key in ("entrance", "exit", "transition", "effects", "params"):
133	        if key in placement:
134	            clip[key] = deepcopy(placement[key])
135	    return clip
136	
137	
138	def _clip_from_run_placement(
139	    placement: dict[str, Any],
140	    run_clip: dict[str, Any],
141	    *,
142	    project_slug: str,
143	    run_id: str,
144	    registry: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
145	    run_registry: banodoco_timeline.AssetRegistry,
146	    root: str | Path | None = None,
147	) -> dict[str, Any]:
148	    clip = deepcopy(run_clip)
149	    clip["id"] = placement["id"]
150	    clip["track"] = placement["track"]
151	    clip["at"] = placement["at"]
152	    if "from_" in clip and "from" not in clip:
153	        clip["from"] = clip.pop("from_")
154	    for key in ("from", "to"):
155	        if key in placement:
156	            clip[key] = placement[key]
157	    for key in ("entrance", "exit", "transition", "effects", "params"):
158	        if key in placement:
159	            clip[key] = deepcopy(placement[key])
160	    asset_key = clip.get("asset")
161	    if isinstance(asset_key, str) and asset_key:
162	        assets = run_registry.get("assets", {})
163	        if asset_key not in assets:
164	            raise FileNotFoundError(
165	                f"asset {asset_key!r} referenced by clip {run_clip.get('id')!r} was not found in run {run_id} assets.json. "
166	                f"Next command: inspect {paths.run_assets_path(project_slug, run_id, root=root)}"
167	            )
168	        namespaced_key = f"run:{run_id}:{asset_key}"
169	        registry[namespaced_key] = deepcopy(assets[asset_key])
170	        clip["asset"] = namespaced_key
171	    return clip
172	
173	
174	def write_materialized_project_timeline(
175	    project_slug: str,
176	    out_dir: str | Path,
177	    *,
178	    root: str | Path | None = None,
179	    theme: str = DEFAULT_THEME,
180	) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
181	    config, registry = materialize_project_timeline(project_slug, root=root, theme=theme)
182	    output = Path(out_dir).expanduser().resolve()
183	    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
184	    timeline_path = output / "hype.timeline.json"
185	    assets_path = output / "hype.assets.json"
186	    banodoco_timeline.save_timeline(config, timeline_path)
187	    banodoco_timeline.save_registry(registry, assets_path)
188	    return timeline_path, assets_path
189	
190

192	    "ProjectMaterializeError",
193	    "materialize_project_timeline",
194	    "materialize_project_timeline_payload",
195	    "require_run_clip",
196	    "write_materialized_project_timeline",
197	]
198
```
