```
import {
  buildGenerateSequenceMessages,
  extractSequenceDrafts,
} from "./templates.ts";
import {
  TRUSTED_SEQUENCE_METADATA,
  TRUSTED_SEQUENCE_CLIP_TYPES,
  validateSequenceDraft,
  type SequenceDraftValidationError,
} from "./sequence-validation.ts";

const ANTHROPIC_MODEL = "claude-opus-4-6";
const ANTHROPIC_URL = "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages";
const ANTHROPIC_TIMEOUT_MS = 150_000;

interface LLMResponse {
  content: string;
  model: string;
}

const buildRepairMessages = (
  originalContent: string,
  allowedClipTypes: readonly string[],
  allowedAssetKeys: readonly string[],
): Array<{ role: string; content: string }> => [
  {
    role: "system",
    content: [
      "You repair malformed Reigh sequence draft responses.",
      "Return JSON only, with shape {\"drafts\":[{\"clipType\":string,\"hold\":number,\"params\":object}]}.",
      "Do not include analysis, explanations, Markdown, or text before or after the JSON.",
      "Use only the allowed clipType values and allowed asset keys.",
    ].join("\n"),
  },
  {
    role: "user",
    content: JSON.stringify({
      malformed_response: originalContent.slice(0, 8000),
      allowed_clip_types: allowedClipTypes,
      allowed_asset_keys: allowedAssetKeys,
    }),
  },
];

const asStringArray = (value: unknown): string[] => {
  return Array.isArray(value)
    ? value.filter((item): item is string => typeof item === "string" && item.trim().length > 0)
    : [];
};

const collectAssetKeys = (...sources: unknown[]): string[] => {
  const keys = new Set<string>();
  for (const source of sources) {
    if (!Array.isArray(source)) continue;
    for (const item of source) {
      if (typeof item === "string" && item.trim()) {
        keys.add(item);
      } else if (item && typeof item === "object") {
        const record = item as Record<string, unknown>;
        for (const field of ["assetKey", "asset_key", "asset", "id", "key"]) {
          const value = record[field];
          if (typeof value === "string" && value.trim()) {
            keys.add(value);
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return [...keys];
};

async function callAnthropic(
  messages: Array<{ role: string; content: string }>,
  logger: { info: (msg: string) => void },
): Promise<LLMResponse> {
  const apiKey = Deno.env.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY");
  if (!apiKey) throw new Error("[ai-generate-sequence] Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY");

  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), ANTHROPIC_TIMEOUT_MS);
  const systemContent = messages.find((message) => message.role === "system")?.content;
  const chatMessages = messages.filter((message) => message.role !== "system");

  try {
    const startedAt = Date.now();
    logger.info(`[AI-GENERATE-SEQUENCE] Anthropic streaming request: model=${ANTHROPIC_MODEL}`);
    const response = await fetch(ANTHROPIC_URL, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "x-api-key": apiKey,
        "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        model: ANTHROPIC_MODEL,
        max_tokens: 4096,
        temperature: 0.3,
        ...(systemContent ? { system: systemContent } : {}),
        messages: chatMessages,
        stream: true,
      }),
      signal: controller.signal,
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      const text = await response.text().catch(() => "");
      throw new Error(`Anthropic ${response.status}: ${text.slice(0, 500)}`);
    }

    const reader = response.body!.getReader();
    const decoder = new TextDecoder();
    let content = "";
    let buffer = "";
    while (true) {
      const { done, value } = await reader.read();
      if (done) break;
      buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
      const lines = buffer.split("\n");
      buffer = lines.pop() ?? "";
      for (const line of lines) {
        if (!line.startsWith("data: ")) continue;
        const data = line.slice(6).trim();
        try {
          const chunk = JSON.parse(data);
          if (chunk.type === "content_block_delta" && chunk.delta?.type === "text_delta") {
            content += chunk.delta.text;
          }
        } catch {
          // Ignore malformed SSE chunks.
        }
      }
    }
    content = content.trim();
    logger.info(`[AI-GENERATE-SEQUENCE] Anthropic response in ${Date.now() - startedAt}ms, model=${ANTHROPIC_MODEL}, length=${content.length}`);
    return { content, model: ANTHROPIC_MODEL };
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timeout);
  }
}
```

```
// Sprint 8 (SD-027 + SD-034): render-button routing.
//
// Decides whether the user's "Render" click should:
//   * stay in the existing client-side WebCodecs path (`useClientRender`),
//     which handles pure-media + Reigh-native clipTypes ("text",
//     "effect-layer", "media", "hold").
//   * delegate to the new orchestrator `banodoco_render_timeline` task,
//     which the banodoco-worker pool services with Node + Chromium +
//     Remotion + the @banodoco/timeline-theme-* packages.
//
// Decision rule (per sprint brief):
//   * If ANY clip's clipType is in THEME_PACKAGE_REGISTRY → orchestrator.
//   * Mixed timelines (themed + media) → orchestrator (option (a)
//     in the architecture doc; uniform composition end-to-end inside
//     the worker, no cross-task ffmpeg-join).
//   * Pure-Reigh-native timelines → client-side render (untouched).
//
// The router is shape-driven — it inspects the resolved TimelineConfig
// and returns a tagged decision. The caller (UI hook) translates that
// decision into either a `useClientRender` invocation or an
// `enqueueBanodocoRenderTimeline` POST.
//
// We intentionally do NOT inspect `timeline.theme` — a timeline can
// declare a theme but only contain pure-media clips, and the existing
// client renderer can still handle that. The trigger is the clipType
// dispatch, not theme presence.

import {
  THEME_PACKAGE_REGISTRY,
  type ThemePackageClipType,
} from '@banodoco/timeline-composition/registry.generated';
import {
  getGeneratedRemotionModuleStatus,
  type GeneratedRemotionModuleBlockReason,
  type GeneratedLaneClipShape,
} from '@/tools/video-editor/lib/generated-lanes';
import { materializeSequenceConfig } from '@/tools/video-editor/sequences/materialize';

/** Minimal clip shape we need from the resolved timeline. */
export interface RouterClipShape extends GeneratedLaneClipShape {
  clipType?: string;
}

/** Minimal timeline shape we need from the resolved config. */
export interface RouterTimelineShape {
  clips?: ReadonlyArray<RouterClipShape> | null;
}

export type RenderRoute = 'client' | 'banodoco' | 'blocked';
```

## Summary of Gaps

Based on my analysis of the sprint-08 implementation versus the epic doc, here are the concrete gaps:

**1. Worker Task Reception Model is Underspecified**
Sprint-08 expects AA's worker to integrate with the Banodoco orchestrator's task-pool mechanism. The `delegateToBanodocoAgent` tool enqueues to `ORCHESTRATOR_TASK_ENQUEUE_URL` with `task_type="banodoco_timeline_generate"`, `worker_pool="banodoco"`, and `run_type="banodoco-worker"` (delegateToBanodocoAgent.ts:160-167). The doc mentions "AA worker for delegated tasks" and "dispatcher by intent," but does not specify:
  - HTTP endpoint signature AA's worker must expose to receive tasks from the orchestrator
  - Whether the orchestrator pushes tasks to a webhook, or AA polls a queue endpoint
  - Required request/response envelope shape for task acknowledgment
  - How correlation_id and expected_version flow through the worker's result callback
  
The polling model exists (`pollBanodocoTaskStatus` in delegateToBanodocoAgent.ts:242-300), but AA's side of writing task status/results is not explained. **File: supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/tools/delegateToBanodocoAgent.ts:113-120, 160-167**

**2. JWT Provisioning & Scope Gaps**
The doc says "user JWT for intent, service-role for write" and that the orchestrator passes user JWT in the task envelope. But missing:
  - Where does AA's worker _get_ the user JWT if it's not in the task envelope? The payload carries `user_jwt` (delegateToBanodocoAgent.ts:45), but does the orchestrator embed it, or does AA need to look it up?
  - What JWT scopes does AA actually need? The auth.ts shows JWTs are verified via `supabaseAdmin.auth.getUser(token)`, checking role != "service_role", but what if the JWT expires mid-task in AA's worker? No retry or refresh strategy is documented.
  - Service-role key provisioning: how does AA's worker securely store the SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY? The doc doesn't mention.
  
**File: supabase/functions/_shared/auth.ts:69-90 (JWT verification), delegateToBanodocoAgent.ts:45 (payload carries user_jwt)**

**3. Render Output Storage & Lifecycle Not Addressed**
Sprint-08 shipped `render-outputs` bucket with a write contract: `<user_id>/<timeline_id>/<task_id>.mp4` via RLS keyed on `auth.uid()` (commit 058d960d3). The doc mentions "render-router + render-outputs storage bucket" exist but doesn't say:
  - Does AA's render worker write MP4s to `render-outputs` bucket, or somewhere else?
  - What's the signed-URL or upload contract? Supabase Storage multipart upload, or direct write via edge function?
  - What metadata does AA write to accompany the render? The tasks table has `result_data` JSON carrying `{artifact_url, correlation_id, content_sha256}` per the render-router code (renderRouter.ts:176-180).
  - Render lifecycle status: `queued` → `In Progress` → `Complete` / `Failed`. Where does AA write these states — to tasks table directly, or via orchestrator callback?

**File: src/tools/video-editor/lib/renderRouter.ts:176-180 (payload shape), supabase/migrations/20260428130000_create_render_outputs_bucket.sql (bucket RLS)**

**4. Sequence Draft Materialization Contract Incomplete**
Sprint-08 has `sequences/materialize.ts` that resolves asset keys in sequence params to URLs. The doc says AA "may receive sequence-shaped requests" and should "materialize via applySequenceDraftToTimeline," but:
  - What is the exact shape of a `SequenceDraft` in the task envelope? The `ai-generate-sequence` edge function validates drafts via Zod, but AA needs the same validation schema to know what to generate.
  - Does AA generate raw sequence JSON, or does it use reigh-app's sequence templates (see `ai-generate-sequence/templates.ts`)? The doc doesn't clarify the boundary.
  - How does AA know which sequence clipTypes are "available" (i.e., registered in `AVAILABLE_SEQUENCE_METADATA`)? The registry is in reigh-app; AA needs to either mirror it or query it.

**File: src/tools/video-editor/sequences/materialize.ts, supabase/functions/ai-generate-sequence/sequence-validation.ts**

**5. DataProvider Contract Underspecifies Asset Upload & Resolution**
The doc says AA implements a `DataProvider`, referencing the interface. The interface has `uploadAsset()`, `registerAsset()`, and `resolveAssetUrl()`, but:
  - Where does AA store uploaded assets? The doc says "source asset (e.g., a video clip from a generation), where does it go? Reigh-app's `generations` table? `render-outputs` bucket? Some other bucket?"
  - What's the relationship between an `AssetRegistryEntry`'s `file` field and Supabase Storage? Is `file` a storage path, a signed URL, or a local key?
  - `uploadAsset()` returns `{assetId, entry: AssetRegistryEntry}`. Does AA's worker call this during task execution, or does AA's CLI only call it?
  - Error semantics: what does AA do if upload fails mid-task?

**File: src/tools/video-editor/data/DataProvider.ts:5-62 (interface), timeline-import/handler.ts:159-170 (asset registry written alongside timeline)**

**6. Reigh-data-fetch Discovery & Pagination Not Spelled Out**
The doc says AA reads via `reigh-data-fetch` but doesn't specify:
  - Does `reigh-data-fetch` return a full project snapshot, or paginated/filtered results?
  - For a given project_id, does it return all timelines, or only the "current" one?
  - Are there separate endpoints for shots vs. generations vs. tasks, or one unified fetch?
  - What does a "full timeline row" include — just config + asset_registry, or also generated assets, task history, etc.?
  - Rate limits: the `ai-generate-sequence` edge function enforces `RATE_LIMITS` (ai-generate-sequence/index.ts:13). Does `reigh-data-fetch` have the same?

**File: supabase/functions/reigh-data-fetch/index.ts:1-100 (structure shows projects / shots / generations / tasks fetches are separate, not unified)**

**7. Versioning Semantics & Conflict Recovery Vague**
The doc says "honor `expected_version`, retry on conflict, cap N=3." But:
  - Is version incremented on _every_ timeline write, or only on certain operations (e.g., clip add, clip delete, not metadata edits)?
  - What happens if AA's worker retries and the user has edited the timeline mid-flight? Does AA re-fetch, reapply ops, and retry? The doc mentions this as "re-fetch, re-apply ops, re-push" but doesn't say how AA detects which ops are AA's vs. user's.
  - Does `correlation_id` alone guarantee idempotency, or does the orchestrator also use `expected_version` for dedup?

**File: timeline-import/handler.ts:126-200 (versioning via RPC), delegateToBanodocoAgent.ts:82-92 (payload carries both correlation_id and expected_version)**

**8. Render Router Classification Missing from Execution Plan**
Sprint-08's `decideRenderRoute()` (commit 058d960d3) classifies timelines into `client` vs `banodoco` render paths based on clipType registry membership. The doc doesn't mention:
  - Must AA's worker implement the same router logic to reject unsupported clipTypes? Or does the orchestrator pre-validate?
  - If AA receives a render task for a timeline with unknown clipTypes, what's the failure mode? Return "failed" status with reason?
  - Does AA's Python client need to import the Remotion renderer (`@banodoco/timeline-composition`), or just orchestrate it server-side?

**File: src/tools/video-editor/lib/renderRouter.ts:30-140 (classification logic)**

**9. Testing Fixtures & Public SDK Acceptance Tests**
Sprint-08's latest commit (f3eceac59) added:
  - `lib/fixtures.ts`: `createAgentWorkflowTimelineFixture()` and `createEmbedDemoTimelineFixture()` 
  - `public-sdk.acceptance.test.ts`: contract tests for the public SDK surface
  - These are exported from `testing.ts` and marked `@publicContract`

The doc says AA can "use these directly for parity tests" but doesn't explain _how_: does AA import the fixtures via npm, or copy them? Are they Remotion-specific or framework-agnostic?

**File: src/tools/video-editor/testing.ts, src/tools/video-editor/lib/fixtures.ts**

**10. Realtime Subscription Channel for Task Status Not Documented**
The doc says "the editor's realtime subscription picks up changes" and "worker writes timeline change," implying a Supabase realtime channel. But:
  - What channel does AA's worker update to trigger the editor's refresh? `timelines:id=<timeline_id>`? Or is there a separate `tasks` channel?
  - Does AA write directly to the `timelines` table row (which Supabase broadcasts), or to a separate status table?
  - How long should reigh-app's UI wait for realtime before timing out?

**Not explicitly documented in sprint-08 code, inferred from Supabase realtime patterns.**

## Top 5 Things the Doc Needs to Add or Expand On

1. **Worker Task Reception & Orchestrator Integration**: Specify the HTTP contract AA's worker exposes (endpoint path, request/response shape), whether tasks are pushed or polled, and how AA writes task status/results back to the orchestrator's state machine.

2. **JWT Provisioning & Management**: Document where/how AA's worker acquires the user JWT, what scopes it needs, how to handle JWT expiration mid-task, and where to securely store the SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.

3. **Asset Storage & Upload Contract**: Define the bucket/path structure where AA stores generated assets (render outputs, source clips, etc.), the upload mechanism (signed URLs, multipart, edge function), and the relationship between AssetRegistry entries and Supabase Storage.

4. **Render Lifecycle & Status Surfacing**: Map out the full render task lifecycle (queued → running → complete/failed), where AA writes each state transition, and how the metadata (artifact_url, correlation_id, content_sha256) flows through the tasks table.

5. **Sequence Contract & Registry**: Provide the exact SequenceDraft JSON schema AA must generate, clarify whether AA needs to mirror/query reigh-app's sequence registries (AVAILABLE_SEQUENCE_METADATA), and specify how unknown sequence clipTypes are handled.

## Bug 1: `pollBanodocoTaskStatus` ↔ task-status edge function mismatch

**The poller** (`supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/tools/delegateToBanodocoAgent.ts`, function `pollBanodocoTaskStatus` ~line 242) calls:
- `GET ${ORCHESTRATOR_BASE_URL}/functions/v1/task-status?task_id=...`
- Expects response body with `{status, correlation_id?, message?, failure_code?, result: {config_version?, ...}}`

**The deployed function** is `supabase/functions/get-task-status/` (POST-only, returns just `{status}`). There's no `task-status` GET endpoint.

**Fix** (cleanest path): Create a new edge function `supabase/functions/task-status/` that:
- Accepts `GET ?task_id=<uuid>` (with `Authorization: Bearer <user_jwt>`)
- Returns `{status, correlation_id?, message?, failure_code?, result?: {config_version?, timeline_id?, ...}}` populated from the `tasks` row's `result_data` JSON column (which already exists in the schema; see `supabase/functions/update-task-status/` for the column it writes to)
- Uses the same JWT verification + ownership-check pattern as `timeline-import/handler.ts` (check `_shared/auth.ts` and `_shared/edgeHandler.ts`)

Don't delete `get-task-status` — it may be used elsewhere. Just add the new function alongside.

## Bug 2: `update-task-status` doesn't surface `config_version` / `correlation_id`

The poller expects `result.config_version` and `correlation_id` in the status response. For task-status to populate those, `update-task-status` (or the new `task-status` reader) needs access to a result envelope written by the worker.

```
2	import { serve } from "https://deno.land/std@0.224.0/http/server.ts";
3	import { withEdgeRequest } from "../_shared/edgeHandler.ts";

6	import { authorizeTaskActor } from "../_shared/taskActorPolicy.ts";
7	
8	/**
9	 * Edge function: get-task-status
10	 *
11	 * Returns the current status of a task by ID.
12	 *
13	 * - Service-role key: can fetch any task
14	 * - User token: can only fetch tasks from their own projects
15	 */
16	serve((req) => {
17	
18	  return withEdgeRequest(req, {
19	    functionName: "get-task-status",
20	    logPrefix: "[GET-TASK-STATUS]",
21	    parseBody: "strict",
22	    auth: {
23	      required: true,
24	    },
25	  }, async ({ supabaseAdmin, logger, body, auth }) => {
26	    const authResult = ensureTaskActor(auth, logger);
27	    if (!authResult.ok) return authResult.response;
28	
29	    const taskId = normalizeTaskId(body.task_id);
30	    if (!taskId) {
31	      logger.error("Missing task_id");
32	      return jsonResponse({ error: "task_id is required" }, 400);
33	    }
34	
35	    logger.setDefaultTaskId(taskId);
36	
37	    const actor = await authorizeTaskActor({
38	      supabaseAdmin,
39	      taskId,
40	      auth: auth!,
41	      logPrefix: "[GET-TASK-STATUS]",
42	    });
43	    if (!actor.ok) {
44	      logger.error("Task access denied", {
45	        task_id: taskId,
46	        error: actor.error,
47	        status_code: actor.statusCode,
48	      });
49	      return jsonResponse({ error: actor.error }, actor.statusCode);
50	    }
51	
52	    const { data: task, error: taskError } = await supabaseAdmin
53	      .from("tasks")
54	      .select("id, status")
55	      .eq("id", taskId)
56	      .single();
57	
58	    if (taskError || !task) {
59	      logger.error("Task not found", { error: taskError?.message });
60	      return jsonResponse({ error: "Task not found" }, 404);
61	    }
62	
63	    logger.info("Returning task status", { status: task.status });
64	    return jsonResponse({ status: task.status }, 200);
65	  });
66	});
```

```
41	  );
42	}

44	export async function handleTimelineImport(
45	  input: HandleTimelineImportInput,
46	): Promise<HandleTimelineImportResult> {
47	  const { body, userId, supabaseAdmin, logger, verifyOwnership } = input;
48	
49	  if (!isUuid(body.project_id)) {
50	    return { status: 400, body: { ok: false, error: "project_id must be a uuid" } };
51	  }
52	  if (!isUuid(body.timeline_id)) {
53	    return { status: 400, body: { ok: false, error: "timeline_id must be a uuid" } };
54	  }
55	  const projectId = body.project_id;
56	  const timelineId = body.timeline_id;
57	  const createIfMissing = body.create_if_missing === true;
58	  const expectedVersionRaw = body.expected_version;
59	  const expectedVersion =
60	    typeof expectedVersionRaw === "number" && Number.isFinite(expectedVersionRaw)
61	      ? Math.trunc(expectedVersionRaw)
62	      : null;
63	
64	  // Shape-validate the timeline against the canonical Zod schema before
65	  // doing anything else. Reigh's runtime treats unknown clipTypes with the
66	  // loud-placeholder fallback, so we purposely do NOT enforce the strict
67	  // effect-id registry here — that's the authoring surface's job.
68	  const parsed = TimelineConfigSchema.safeParse(body.timeline);
69	  if (!parsed.success) {
70	    return {
71	      status: 400,
72	      body: {
73	        ok: false,
74	        error: "timeline payload failed schema validation",
75	        details: parsed.error.message,
76	      },
77	    };
78	  }
79	  const validated = validateTimelinePayload(body);
80	  if (!validated.ok) {
81	    return {
82	      status: 400,
83	      body: { ok: false, error: validated.error },
84	    };
85	  }
86	
87	  // Ownership check: the JWT subject must own the project. SD-022: the user
88	  // JWT authorizes intent; the service-role key is then used for the actual
89	  // DB write below. authenticateRequest() already verified the JWT and gave
90	  // us userId; verifyProjectOwnership compares against projects.user_id.
91	  const ownership = await verifyOwnership(projectId, userId);
92	  if (!ownership.success) {
93	    return {
94	      status: ownership.statusCode ?? 403,
95	      body: {
96	        ok: false,
97	        error: ownership.error ?? "Forbidden",
98	      },
99	    };
100	  }
101	
102	  // Lookup current row + version. We need this for: (a) 404/create_if_missing
103	  // branching, (b) timeline.project_id ownership check, (c) --force fetch.
104	  const { data: existing, error: lookupError } = await supabaseAdmin
105	    .from("timelines")
106	    .select("id, project_id, config_version")
107	    .eq("id", timelineId)
108	    .maybeSingle();

110	  if (lookupError) {

112	    return {

114	      body: { ok: false, error: "failed to load timeline", details: lookupError.message },
115	    };
116	  }
117	
118	  if (!existing) {
119	    if (!createIfMissing) {
120	      return {
121	        status: 404,
122	        body: { ok: false, error: "timeline not found" },
123	      };
124	    }
125	    return await insertNewTimeline({
126	      supabaseAdmin,

130	      timelineConfig: validated.timeline,
131	      assetRegistry: validated.assetRegistry,
132	    });
133	  }
134	
135	  if (existing.project_id !== projectId) {
136	    return {

138	      body: {

140	        error: "timeline belongs to a different project",
141	      },
142	    };
143	  }
144	
145	  // Version handshake. expected_version is omitted on --force; we then
146	  // adopt the current version as the expected value (last-write-wins).
147	  const versionToSend = expectedVersion ?? existing.config_version;
148	
149	  return await callVersionedRpc({
150	    supabaseAdmin,
151	    logger,

153	    timelineConfig: validated.timeline,
154	    assetRegistry: validated.assetRegistry,
155	    expectedVersion: versionToSend,
156	    currentVersion: existing.config_version,
157	  });

167	}

169	async function insertNewTimeline(
170	  input: InsertNewTimelineInput,
171	): Promise<HandleTimelineImportResult> {
172	  const { supabaseAdmin, logger, projectId, timelineId, timelineConfig, assetRegistry } = input;
173	  const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin
174	    .from("timelines")
175	    .insert({
176	      id: timelineId,
177	      project_id: projectId,
178	      config: timelineConfig,
179	      asset_registry: assetRegistry ?? { assets: {} },
180	      config_version: 1,
181	    })
182	    .select("config_version")
183	    .single();
184	  if (error) {
185	    logger.error("timeline insert failed", { error: error.message });
186	    return {
187	      status: 500,
188	      body: { ok: false, error: "timeline insert failed", details: error.message },
189	    };
190	  }
191	  return {
192	    status: 201,
193	    body: {
194	      ok: true,
195	      config_version: typeof data?.config_version === "number" ? data.config_version : 1,
196	      created: true,
197	    },
198	  };
199	}
200	
201	interface CallVersionedRpcInput {
202	  supabaseAdmin: SupabaseClient;
203	  logger: Logger;
204	  timelineId: string;
205	  timelineConfig: Record<string, unknown>;
206	  assetRegistry: Record<string, unknown> | null;
207	  expectedVersion: number;
208	  currentVersion: number;
209	}
210	
211	async function callVersionedRpc(
212	  input: CallVersionedRpcInput,
213	): Promise<HandleTimelineImportResult> {
214	  const {
215	    supabaseAdmin,
216	    logger,
217	    timelineId,
218	    timelineConfig,
219	    assetRegistry,
220	    expectedVersion,
221	    currentVersion,
222	  } = input;
223	  const useAssetVariant = assetRegistry !== null;
224	  const rpcName = useAssetVariant
225	    ? "update_timeline_versioned"
226	    : "update_timeline_config_versioned";
227	  const params = useAssetVariant
228	    ? {
229	      p_timeline_id: timelineId,
230	      p_expected_version: expectedVersion,
231	      p_config: timelineConfig,
232	      p_asset_registry: assetRegistry,
233	    }
234	    : {
235	      p_timeline_id: timelineId,
236	      p_expected_version: expectedVersion,
237	      p_config: timelineConfig,
238	    };
239	  const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin.rpc(rpcName as never, params as never);
240	  if (error) {
241	    logger.error("versioned rpc failed", { error: error.message, rpc: rpcName });
242	    return {
243	      status: 500,
244	      body: { ok: false, error: "rpc failed", details: error.message },
245	    };
246	  }
247	  const rows = (data ?? []) as Array<{ config_version: number }>;
248	  if (rows.length === 0) {
249	    return {
250	      status: 409,
251	      body: { ok: false, error: "version_mismatch", current_version: currentVersion },
252	    };
253	  }
254	  return {
255	    status: 200,
256	    body: { ok: true, config_version: rows[0].config_version, created: false },
257	  };
258	}
```

```
4	import { jsonResponse } from "../_shared/http.ts";

6	import { handleTimelineImport } from "./handler.ts";
7	import type { TimelineImportBody } from "./types.ts";
8	
9	/**
10	 * Sprint 6 (Phase 6): import a Banodoco-authored timeline + asset registry
11	 * into a Reigh project.
12	 *
13	 * Auth: reuses `_shared/auth.ts:authenticateRequest()` via withEdgeRequest;
14	 * `allowJwtUserAuth: true` so Supabase user JWTs from the publish CLI are
15	 * accepted. Service-role keys are also accepted (for orchestrator paths).
16	 *
17	 * Concurrency: writes go through `update_timeline_config_versioned` (or
18	 * `update_timeline_versioned` when an asset registry is in the payload).
19	 * `expected_version` is required unless `--force` is set on the CLI; on a
20	 * `--force` request we read the current version inside the function and
21	 * use it as the expected value (last-write-wins semantics).
22	 */
23	serve((req) =>
24	  withEdgeRequest<TimelineImportBody>(
25	    req,
26	    {
27	      functionName: "timeline-import",
28	      logPrefix: "[TIMELINE-IMPORT]",
29	      method: "POST",
30	      parseBody: "strict",
31	      auth: { required: true, options: { allowJwtUserAuth: true } },
32	      ...NO_SESSION_RUNTIME_OPTIONS,
33	    },
34	    async ({ auth, body, logger, supabaseAdmin }) => {
35	      // Service-role callers don't carry a user identity. The publish CLI
36	      // path requires a user JWT; reject service-role here to keep the
37	      // ownership invariant simple. The orchestrator can mint a JWT if it
38	      // ever needs to publish on a user's behalf.
39	      if (!auth?.userId) {
40	        return jsonResponse({ error: "user JWT required (service-role not accepted on this path)" }, 401);
41	      }
42	
43	      const result = await handleTimelineImport({
44	        body,
45	        userId: auth.userId,
46	        supabaseAdmin,
47	        logger,
48	        verifyOwnership: (projectId, userId) =>
49	          verifyProjectOwnership(supabaseAdmin, projectId, userId, "[TIMELINE-IMPORT]"),
50	      });
51	
52	      return jsonResponse(result.body, result.status);
53	    },
54	  )
55	);
```

```
1	import type { UpdateTaskStatusRequest } from './types.ts';
2	
3	export function buildTaskUpdatePayload(request: UpdateTaskStatusRequest): Record<string, unknown> {
4	  const payload: Record<string, unknown> = {
5	    status: request.status,
6	    updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
7	  };
8	
9	  if (request.status === 'In Progress') {
10	    payload.generation_started_at = new Date().toISOString();
11	  }
12	
13	  if (request.reset_generation_started_at === true) {
14	    payload.generation_started_at = new Date().toISOString();
15	  }
16	
17	  if (request.status === 'Complete') {
18	    payload.generation_processed_at = new Date().toISOString();
19	  }
20	
21	  if (request.output_location !== undefined) {
22	    payload.output_location = request.output_location;
23	  }
24	
25	  if (request.attempts !== undefined) {
26	    payload.attempts = request.attempts;
27	  }
28	
29	  if (request.error_details !== undefined) {
30	    payload.error_message = request.error_details;
31	  }
32	
33	  if (request.clear_worker === true) {
34	    payload.worker_id = null;
35	    payload.generation_started_at = null;
36	  }
37	
38	  return payload;
39	}
```

```
132	/**
133	 * Shared bootstrap for edge handlers:
134	 * - OPTIONS short-circuit
135	 * - method guard
136	 * - runtime initialization
137	 * - optional JSON body parsing
138	 * - optional authentication + service-role policy
139	 */
140	export async function bootstrapEdgeHandler<TBody extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, unknown>>(
141	  req: Request,
142	  options: EdgeBootstrapOptions,
143	): Promise<EdgeBootstrapResult<TBody>> {
144	  const method = methodFor(options);
145	  const format = errorFormat(options);
146	  const corsPreflight = options.corsPreflight ?? true;
147	
148	  if (corsPreflight && req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
149	    return {
150	      ok: false,
151	      response: jsonResponse({ ok: true }),
152	    };
153	  }
154	
155	  const runtimeResult = initEdgeRuntime(
156	    options.functionName,
157	    options.logPrefix,
158	    options.runtimeOptions,
159	  );
160	  if (!runtimeResult.ok) {
161	    return {
162	      ok: false,
163	      response: operationFailureResponse(runtimeResult, 500),
164	    };
165	  }
166	
167	  const { supabaseAdmin, logger } = runtimeResult.value;
168	
169	  if (req.method !== method) {
170	    logger.warn('Method not allowed', { method: req.method });
171	    await logger.flush();
172	    return {
173	      ok: false,
174	      response: buildErrorResponse('Method not allowed', 405, format, { Allow: method }),
175	    };
176	  }
177	
178	  let body: Record<string, unknown> = {};
179	
180	  if (parseMode(options) === 'strict') {
181	    const parsedBody = await parseJsonBodyStrict(req, logger, {
182	      message: options.invalidJsonMessage,
183	      nonObjectMessage: options.invalidJsonShapeMessage,
184	    });
185	    if (!parsedBody.ok) {
186	      return {
187	        ok: false,
188	        response: format === 'text'
189	          ? buildErrorResponse(parsedBody.message, 400, 'text')
190	          : parseJsonFailureResponse(parsedBody),
191	      };
192	    }
193	    body = parsedBody.value;
194	  } else if (parseMode(options) === 'loose') {
195	    const parsedBody = await parseJsonBody(req, logger, {
196	      mode: 'loose',
197	      message: options.invalidJsonMessage,
198	      nonObjectMessage: options.invalidJsonShapeMessage,
199	    });
200	    if (!parsedBody.ok) {
201	      return {
202	        ok: false,
203	        response: format === 'text'
204	          ? buildErrorResponse(parsedBody.message, 400, 'text')
205	          : parseJsonFailureResponse(parsedBody),
206	      };
207	    }
208	    body = parsedBody.value;
209	  }
210	
211	  let auth: AuthResult | null = null;
212	  if (authIsRequired(options)) {
213	    auth = await authenticateRequest(
214	      req,
215	      supabaseAdmin,
216	      options.logPrefix,
217	      options.auth?.options ?? {},
218	    );
219	    if (!auth.success) {
220	      return {
221	        ok: false,
222	        response: buildErrorResponse(
223	          auth.error || 'Authentication failed',
224	          auth.statusCode || 401,
225	          format,
226	        ),
227	      };
228	    }
229	
230	    if (options.auth?.requireServiceRole && !auth.isServiceRole) {
231	      return {
232	        ok: false,
233	        response: buildErrorResponse('Unauthorized - service role required', 403, format),
234	      };
235	    }
236	  }
237	
238	  return {
239	    ok: true,
240	    value: {
241	      req,
242	      body: body as TBody,
243	      supabaseAdmin,
244	      logger,
245	      auth,
246	    },
247	  };
248	}
249	
250	/**
251	 * High-level request wrapper that standardizes edge endpoint choreography:
252	 * bootstrap -> handler -> unified unexpected-error response -> guaranteed flush.
253	 */
254	export async function withEdgeRequest<TBody extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, unknown>>(
255	  req: Request,
256	  options: EdgeBootstrapOptions,
257	  handler: (context: EdgeRequestContext<TBody>) => Promise<Response>,
258	): Promise<Response> {
259	  const bootstrap = await bootstrapEdgeHandler<TBody>(req, options);
260	  if (!bootstrap.ok) {
261	    return bootstrap.response;
262	  }
263	
264	  const context = bootstrap.value;
265	  try {
266	    return await handler(context);
267	  } catch (error: unknown) {
268	    context.logger.critical('Unexpected error', {
269	      error: toErrorMessage(error),
270	    });
271	    return buildErrorResponse('Internal server error', 500, errorFormat(options));
272	  } finally {
273	    await context.logger.flush();
274	  }
275	}
```

```
80	export function ensureOwnedStoragePath(
81	  storagePath: unknown,
82	  userId: string,
83	  logger: GuardLogger,
84	): GuardResult<StoragePathGuardResult> {
85	  const normalizedPath =
86	    typeof storagePath === "string"
87	      ? storagePath.trim().replace(/^\/+/, "").replace(/\/+$/, "")
88	      : "";
89	
90	  if (!normalizedPath) {
91	    logger.error("Invalid storage path", { storagePath });
92	    return {
93	      ok: false,
94	      response: jsonResponse({ error: "Invalid storage path" }, 400),
95	    };
96	  }
97	
98	  const segments = normalizedPath.split("/");
99	  if (segments.some((segment) => segment.length === 0 || segment === "." || segment === "..")) {
100	    logger.error("Invalid storage path segments", { storagePath: normalizedPath });
101	    return {
102	      ok: false,
103	      response: jsonResponse({ error: "Invalid storage path" }, 400),
104	    };
105	  }
106	
107	  if (segments[0] !== userId) {
108	    logger.error("Storage path ownership mismatch", {
109	      storagePath: normalizedPath,
110	      userId,
111	    });
112	    return {
113	      ok: false,
114	      response: jsonResponse(
115	        { error: "Forbidden: storage path does not belong to authenticated user" },
116	        403,
117	      ),
118	    };
119	  }
120	
121	  return {
122	    ok: true,
123	    storagePath: normalizedPath,
124	  };
125	}
```

```
246	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
247	// Status polling helper (called from the agent loop on each turn while a
248	// banodoco task is in flight). Pure data shape; the loop wraps it.
249	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
250	
251	export interface BanodocoTaskStatusSnapshot {
252	  task_id: string;
253	  status: "Queued" | "In Progress" | "Complete" | "Failed" | "worker_unavailable" | "unknown";
254	  failure_code?: string;
255	  message?: string;
256	  config_version?: number;
257	  correlation_id?: string;
258	}
259	
260	export async function pollBanodocoTaskStatus(
261	  taskId: string,
262	  userJwt: string,
263	  options: { fetchImpl?: typeof fetch } = {},
264	): Promise<BanodocoTaskStatusSnapshot> {
265	  const orchestratorUrl = Deno.env.get("ORCHESTRATOR_TASK_STATUS_URL")
266	    ?? Deno.env.get("ORCHESTRATOR_BASE_URL");
267	  if (!orchestratorUrl) {
268	    return { task_id: taskId, status: "unknown", message: "ORCHESTRATOR_BASE_URL not set" };
269	  }
270	
271	  const statusUrl = orchestratorUrl.includes("/tasks/")
272	    ? orchestratorUrl
273	    : `${orchestratorUrl.replace(/\/$/, "")}/functions/v1/task-status?task_id=${encodeURIComponent(taskId)}`;
274	
275	  const fetchImpl = options.fetchImpl ?? fetch;
276	  let resp: Response;
277	  try {
278	    resp = await fetchImpl(statusUrl, {
279	      headers: { "Authorization": `Bearer ${userJwt}` },
280	    });
281	  } catch (err) {
282	    return {
283	      task_id: taskId,
284	      status: "unknown",
285	      message: `status fetch failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,
286	    };
287	  }
288	
289	  if (resp.status >= 400) {
290	    return { task_id: taskId, status: "unknown", message: `HTTP ${resp.status}` };
291	  }
292	
293	  let body: unknown = null;
294	  try {
295	    body = await resp.json();
296	  } catch {
297	    return { task_id: taskId, status: "unknown", message: "non-JSON response" };
298	  }
299	
300	  if (!isRecord(body)) {
301	    return { task_id: taskId, status: "unknown" };
302	  }
303	
304	  const status = typeof body.status === "string" ? body.status : "unknown";
305	  const failure_code = typeof body.failure_code === "string" ? body.failure_code : undefined;
306	  const message = typeof body.message === "string" ? body.message : undefined;
307	  const correlation_id = typeof body.correlation_id === "string" ? body.correlation_id : undefined;
308	  const config_version = typeof (body as { result?: unknown }).result === "object"
309	    && isRecord((body as { result?: unknown }).result)
310	    && typeof (body as { result: { config_version?: unknown } }).result.config_version === "number"
311	    ? (body as { result: { config_version: number } }).result.config_version
312	    : undefined;
313	
314	  // Normalise the status enum to the BanodocoTaskStatusSnapshot variant set.
315	  const normalisedStatus: BanodocoTaskStatusSnapshot["status"] =
316	    status === "Queued" || status === "In Progress" || status === "Complete"
317	      || status === "Failed"
318	      ? status
319	      : (failure_code === "worker_unavailable" ? "worker_unavailable" : "unknown");
320	
321	  return {
322	    task_id: taskId,
323	    status: normalisedStatus,
324	    failure_code,
325	    message,
326	    correlation_id,
327	    config_version,
328	  };
329	}
330	
331	export function summariseTaskStatusForChat(snap: BanodocoTaskStatusSnapshot): string {
332	  switch (snap.status) {
333	    case "Queued":
334	      return "Banodoco task is still queued — no worker has claimed it yet.";
335	    case "In Progress":
336	      return "Banodoco worker is generating now.";
337	    case "Complete":
338	      return snap.config_version
339	        ? `Banodoco wrote v${snap.config_version} — the editor's realtime subscription will refresh shortly.`
```

```
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

import { parseAndValidateRequest } from './request.ts';

function createLoggerStub() {
  return {
    error: vi.fn(),
    flush: vi.fn(async () => {}),
  };
}

describe('parseAndValidateRequest', () => {
  it('parses a valid request', async () => {
    const logger = createLoggerStub();
    const req = new Request('http://localhost/update-task-status', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ task_id: 'task-1', status: 'Queued' }),
    });

    const result = await parseAndValidateRequest(req, logger);
    expect(result.ok).toBe(true);
    if (result.ok) {
      expect(result.data.task_id).toBe('task-1');
      expect(result.data.status).toBe('Queued');
    }
  });

  it('rejects invalid JSON', async () => {
    const logger = createLoggerStub();
    const req = new Request('http://localhost/update-task-status', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: '{bad-json',
    });

    const result = await parseAndValidateRequest(req, logger);
    expect(result.ok).toBe(false);
    if (!result.ok) {
      expect(result.response.status).toBe(400);
    }
    expect(logger.error).toHaveBeenCalledWith('Invalid JSON body', undefined);
    expect(logger.flush).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('rejects invalid status values', async () => {
    const logger = createLoggerStub();
    const req = new Request('http://localhost/update-task-status', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ task_id: 'task-1', status: 'pending' }),
    });

    const result = await parseAndValidateRequest(req, logger);
    expect(result.ok).toBe(false);
    if (!result.ok) {
      expect(result.response.status).toBe(400);
    }
    expect(logger.error).toHaveBeenCalledWith('Invalid status value', {
      status: 'pending',
      valid_statuses: expect.any(Array),
    });
    expect(logger.flush).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('rejects malformed attempts type', async () => {
    const logger = createLoggerStub();
    const req = new Request('http://localhost/update-task-status', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ task_id: 'task-1', status: 'Queued', attempts: '3' }),
    });

    const result = await parseAndValidateRequest(req, logger);
    expect(result.ok).toBe(false);
    if (!result.ok) {
      expect(result.response.status).toBe(400);
      const body = JSON.parse(await result.response.text()) as Record<string, unknown>;
      expect(body.message).toBe('attempts must be a number');
    }
    expect(logger.error).toHaveBeenCalledWith('Invalid attempts value', { attempts: '3' });
    expect(logger.flush).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

import { buildTaskUpdatePayload } from './payload.ts';

describe('buildTaskUpdatePayload', () => {
  it('maps common request fields', () => {
    const payload = buildTaskUpdatePayload({
      task_id: 'task-1',
      status: 'Failed',
      output_location: '/tmp/out.png',
      attempts: 3,
      error_details: 'worker crashed',
    });

    expect(payload.status).toBe('Failed');
    expect(typeof payload.updated_at).toBe('string');
    expect(payload.output_location).toBe('/tmp/out.png');
    expect(payload.attempts).toBe(3);
    expect(payload.error_message).toBe('worker crashed');
  });

  it('sets completion timestamp for Complete', () => {
    const payload = buildTaskUpdatePayload({
      task_id: 'task-1',
      status: 'Complete',
    });

    expect(typeof payload.generation_processed_at).toBe('string');
  });

  it('clears worker assignment for requeue', () => {
    const payload = buildTaskUpdatePayload({
      task_id: 'task-1',
      status: 'Queued',
      clear_worker: true,
    });

    expect(payload.worker_id).toBeNull();
    expect(payload.generation_started_at).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

```json
  "content": "// Response shape for the GET task-status endpoint, matching what\n// reigh-app's banodoco poller (`pollBanodocoTaskStatus`) expects.\n//\n// The poller surface is documented at\n// `supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/tools/delegateToBanodocoAgent.ts`\n// (`BanodocoTaskStatusSnapshot`); see also Bug 1 in the cross-repo\n// contract notes. We deliberately keep this lenient: extra fields are\n// allowed in `result` and the worker may surface either snake_case or\n// pass-through values in the `result_data` JSON column.\nexport interface TaskStatusResultEnvelope {\n  config_version?: number;\n  timeline_id?: string;\n  // The poller treats `result` as an open record — workers may add more\n  // fields without coordinating a schema bump.\n  [key: string]: unknown;\n}\n\nexport interface TaskStatusResponseBody {\n  status: string;\n  correlation_id?: string;\n  message?: string;\n  failure_code?: string;\n  result?: TaskStatusResultEnvelope;\n}\n"
}
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/supabase/functions/task-status/handler.ts",
  "content": "// deno-lint-ignore-file\nimport type { SupabaseClient } from \"https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2.49.4\";\nimport type { TaskStatusResponseBody, TaskStatusResultEnvelope } from \"./types.ts\";\n\ninterface Logger {\n  info(message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>): void;\n  warn(message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>): void;\n  error(message: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>): void;\n}\n\nexport interface HandleTaskStatusInput {\n  taskId: string;\n  supabaseAdmin: SupabaseClient;\n  logger: Logger;\n}\n\nexport interface HandleTaskStatusResult {\n  status: number;\n  body: TaskStatusResponseBody | { error: string };\n}\n\nfunction isUuid(value: unknown): value is string {\n  return (\n    typeof value === \"string\" &&\n    /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i.test(value)\n  );\n}\n\nfunction isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {\n  return typeof value === \"object\" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads a task's status row and projects the response envelope expected by\n * the banodoco poller. The `result_data` JSON column holds the worker-supplied\n * envelope (see Bug 2 in the cross-repo contract notes); this handler hoists\n * the well-known fields (correlation_id, message, failure_code) into the\n * top-level response and passes the remaining fields through under `result`.\n *\n * Authentication and ownership are handled by the caller (see ./index.ts):\n * we mirror `timeline-import` and assume `verifyOwnership` has already passed.\n */\nexport async function handleTaskStatus(\n  input: HandleTaskStatusInput,\n): Promise<HandleTaskStatusResult> {\n  const { taskId, supabaseAdmin, logger } = input;\n\n  if (!isUuid(taskId)) {\n    return { status: 400, body: { error: \"task_id must be a uuid\" } };\n  }\n\n  const { data: task, error } = await supabaseAdmin\n    .from(\"tasks\")\n    .select(\"id, status, result_data\")\n    .eq(\"id\", taskId)\n    .maybeSingle();\n\n  if (error) {\n    logger.error(\"task lookup failed\", { error: error.message });\n    return { status: 500, body: { error: \"failed to load task\" } };\n  }\n  if (!task) {\n    return { status: 404, body: { error: \"Task not found\" } };\n  }\n\n  const resultData = isRecord(task.result_data) ? task.result_data : {};\n\n  const correlation_id =\n    typeof resultData.correlation_id === \"string\" ? resultData.correlation_id : undefined;\n  const message = typeof resultData.message === \"string\" ? resultData.message : undefined;\n  const failure_code =\n    typeof resultData.failure_code === \"string\" ? resultData.failure_code : undefined;\n\n  // Everything in result_data that is *not* a top-level surfaced field\n  // becomes the `result` envelope. We keep keys workers care about\n  // (config_version, timeline_id) and forward unknown keys verbatim so\n  // the worker contract stays open-ended.\n  const RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL = new Set([\"correlation_id\", \"message\", \"failure_code\"]);\n  const result: TaskStatusResultEnvelope = {};\n  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(resultData)) {\n    if (RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL.has(key)) continue;\n    result[key] = value;\n  }\n\n  const body: TaskStatusResponseBody = {\n    status: typeof task.status === \"string\" ? task.status : \"unknown\",\n  };\n  if (correlation_id !== undefined) body.correlation_id = correlation_id;\n  if (message !== undefined) body.message = message;\n  if (failure_code !== undefined) body.failure_code = failure_code;\n  if (Object.keys(result).length > 0) body.result = result;\n\n  logger.info(\"Returning task status\", {\n    task_id: taskId,\n    status: body.status,\n    has_result: body.result !== undefined,\n  });\n\n  return { status: 200, body };\n}\n"
}
```

```json
  "content": "// deno-lint-ignore-file\nimport { serve } from \"https://deno.land/std@0.224.0/http/server.ts\";\nimport { NO_SESSION_RUNTIME_OPTIONS, withEdgeRequest } from \"../_shared/edgeHandler.ts\";\nimport { jsonResponse } from \"../_shared/http.ts\";\nimport { ensureTaskActor } from \"../_shared/requestGuards.ts\";\nimport { authorizeTaskActor } from \"../_shared/taskActorPolicy.ts\";\nimport { handleTaskStatus } from \"./handler.ts\";\n\n/**\n * Edge function: task-status (GET)\n *\n * Banodoco-poller-facing read endpoint. Accepts `GET ?task_id=<uuid>` with a\n * `Authorization: Bearer <user_jwt>` (or service-role key) header and returns\n *\n *   { status, correlation_id?, message?, failure_code?, result?: { config_version?, timeline_id?, ... } }\n *\n * which is the contract expected by `pollBanodocoTaskStatus` in\n * `supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/tools/delegateToBanodocoAgent.ts`.\n *\n * The legacy POST-only `get-task-status` function is left in place for any\n * existing callers; this is a separate function so we can ship the GET shape\n * without churning that contract. See the cross-repo contract notes (Bug 1).\n *\n * Auth: reuses `_shared/auth.ts:authenticateRequest()` via `withEdgeRequest`,\n * with `allowJwtUserAuth: true`. Ownership is enforced by `authorizeTaskActor`\n * (service-role bypasses; users must own the task's project).\n */\nserve((req) =>\n  withEdgeRequest(\n    req,\n    {\n      functionName: \"task-status\",\n      logPrefix: \"[TASK-STATUS]\",\n      method: \"GET\",\n      parseBody: \"none\",\n      auth: { required: true, options: { allowJwtUserAuth: true } },\n      ...NO_SESSION_RUNTIME_OPTIONS,\n    },\n    async ({ req, auth, logger, supabaseAdmin }) => {\n      const actorCheck = ensureTaskActor(auth, logger);\n      if (!actorCheck.ok) return actorCheck.response;\n\n      let url: URL;\n      try {\n        url = new URL(req.url);\n      } catch {\n        return jsonResponse({ error: \"invalid request url\" }, 400);\n      }\n\n      const taskId = url.searchParams.get(\"task_id\");\n      if (!taskId) {\n        logger.error(\"Missing task_id query param\");\n        return jsonResponse({ error: \"task_id query parameter is required\" }, 400);\n      }\n\n      logger.setDefaultTaskId(taskId);\n\n      const authorization = await authorizeTaskActor({\n        supabaseAdmin,\n        taskId,\n        auth: auth!,\n        logPrefix: \"[TASK-STATUS]\",\n      });\n      if (!authorization.ok) {\n        logger.error(\"Task access denied\", {\n          task_id: taskId,\n          error: authorization.error,\n          status_code: authorization.statusCode,\n        });\n        return jsonResponse({ error: authorization.error }, authorization.statusCode);\n      }\n\n      const result = await handleTaskStatus({ taskId, supabaseAdmin, logger });\n      return jsonResponse(result.body, result.status);\n    },\n  )\n);\n"
}
```

## Report

**Branch:** `sprint-8-themed-render-via-orchestrator` — committed locally (commit `ee2e6f10c`), not pushed.

**Files changed (11 files, +460 lines):**
- `supabase/functions/task-status/index.ts` (new, ~75 lines) — GET entrypoint, query-param `task_id`, JWT/service-role auth via `withEdgeRequest` + `authorizeTaskActor`.
- `supabase/functions/task-status/handler.ts` (new, ~96 lines) — reads `tasks.{id,status,result_data}`, hoists `correlation_id`/`message`/`failure_code` to top level, passes remaining keys (`config_version`, `timeline_id`, …) through under `result`.
- `supabase/functions/task-status/types.ts` (new, 22 lines) — `TaskStatusResponseBody` matching poller contract.
- `supabase/functions/task-status/handler.test.ts` (new, 132 lines) — 6 tests covering uuid validation, 404, 500, empty result_data, full envelope projection, failure_code path.
- `supabase/functions/update-task-status/{types.ts, request.ts, payload.ts}` — new optional `result_data: Record<string,unknown>` field, validated as JSON object (rejects strings/arrays), written to `tasks.result_data` only when present.
- `supabase/functions/update-task-status/{request.test.ts, payload.test.ts}` — 4 added tests for result_data round-trip + invalid-shape rejection.
- `supabase/functions/vitest.unit.config.ts` and `config/testing/vitest.edge.config.ts` — registered `task-status/**/*.test.ts` in include lists.

**`result_data` column:** already existed; added by migration `20250202000000_add_missing_columns.sql` as `jsonb DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb`. No new migration needed.

**Test results:** `npm run test:edge:unit` — 99 files / **542 tests pass**. Targeted run on changed dirs: 10 files / 47 tests pass. Contract checks (`check:contracts`, `check:contract-surface-map`) pass.

**Constraints honoured:** poller untouched, `get-task-status` untouched, status enum casing untouched (`Queued | In Progress | Complete | Failed | Cancelled`), JWT auth via `_shared/auth.ts` mirroring `timeline-import`. Stale `public/hero-background-loop.mp4` deletion left out of the commit. Not pushed.

**Nothing was skipped.**

> DEVELOPER

Extend reigh-app's `claim-next-task` edge function to support the banodoco worker pool. The reference `banodoco-worker/worker.py` and the orchestrator's `banodoco.py` handler both expect `worker_pool` filtering, but the deployed function ignores it. Without this, banodoco-pool tasks can't actually be claimed by the right worker.

## Repo + branch
`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app`. Local branch `sprint-8-themed-render-via-orchestrator` (commit `ee2e6f10c` is your previous fix). Make a NEW commit on top.

## Files of interest
- `supabase/functions/claim-next-task/index.ts` — the function to extend.
- `supabase/migrations/` — find the underlying `claim_next_task_atomic` (or similarly named) RPC. Likely accepts `p_run_type` already.
- Reference for what banodoco workers send: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/banodoco-workspace/banodoco-worker/worker.py` lines ~88-130 (`_claim_next_task`). Sends `{worker_id, run_type: "banodoco-worker", worker_pool: "banodoco", task_types: [...]}`.
- Reference for orchestrator pool taxonomy: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker-orchestrator/api_orchestrator/handlers/banodoco.py`.
- Tasks the banodoco pool claims: `banodoco_timeline_generate`, `banodoco_render_timeline`.

## What to change

1. **`claim-next-task/index.ts`**:
   - Accept optional `worker_pool: string` and `task_types: string[]` in the request body.
   - Widen `run_type` validation: currently only `'gpu' | 'api'`. Accept `'banodoco-worker'` as a third valid value when `worker_pool === 'banodoco'`. Don't break `gpu`/`api` paths.
   - Pass `worker_pool` and `task_types` through to the underlying RPC call (or filter in JS if the RPC doesn't support it — see step 2).

2. **The RPC** (`claim_next_task_atomic` or similar):
   - Find it in `supabase/migrations/`.
   - If it doesn't support `p_worker_pool` / `p_task_types`, add a NEW migration `supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_extend_claim_next_task_for_pools.sql` that creates a new overload (or extends the existing one) accepting these as optional parameters. Filter the candidate task set by:
     - When `p_task_types` is provided (non-null, non-empty), the task's `task_type` must be in that list.
     - When `p_worker_pool === 'banodoco'`, only return tasks whose `task_type` starts with `banodoco_` (i.e. `banodoco_timeline_generate`, `banodoco_render_timeline`). For other worker_pool values OR null, preserve current behavior.
   - Don't break the existing API/GPU worker call sites.

3. **Tests**:
   - Add tests in `supabase/functions/claim-next-task/index.test.ts` (or wherever tests live for this function) covering:
     - Existing API/GPU paths still work unchanged.
     - With `worker_pool='banodoco'` and `run_type='banodoco-worker'` in the body, the function accepts and forwards both.
     - With `task_types=['banodoco_timeline_generate']`, only that type is claimed.
     - A non-banodoco task type isn't claimed by a banodoco worker.

4. **Status enum and other contracts**: do not change. Leave `update-task-status`, `task-status` (your previous addition), `get-task-status` alone.

## Constraints
- Do NOT modify `banodoco-worker/worker.py` or the orchestrator handlers — they're already correct, the edge function is what's behind.
- Do NOT delete/replace existing functionality — additive only.
- Keep migration filenames lex-sortable to come after existing migrations.
- Run the project's existing test command (`npm run test:edge:unit` per your prior fix) and ensure it still passes.

## When done
Commit with message starting `fix(edge): claim-next-task supports worker_pool + banodoco-worker run_type`. Don't push.

Report back under 250 words:
- Files changed (paths + line counts)
- Whether the RPC needed extension or supported the new params
- Test results (full suite count + any new tests added)
- Anything you couldn't do

```
1	-- Add starvation protection to claim_next_task_service_role via p_max_task_wait_minutes.
2	--
3	-- Workers can still prefer tasks matching their current model, but once any
4	-- eligible queued task has waited past the threshold we fall back to pure FIFO.
5	
6	BEGIN;
7	
8	-- IMPORTANT: drop the old 4-arg overload before creating the 5-arg version.
9	-- CREATE OR REPLACE only replaces identical signatures.
10	DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.claim_next_task_service_role(TEXT, BOOLEAN, TEXT, BOOLEAN);
11	
12	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION claim_next_task_service_role(
13	  p_worker_id TEXT,
14	  p_include_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
15	  p_run_type TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
16	  p_same_model_only BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
17	  p_max_task_wait_minutes INT DEFAULT 5
18	)
19	RETURNS TABLE(
20	  task_id UUID,
21	  params JSONB,
22	  task_type TEXT,
23	  project_id UUID,
24	  user_id UUID
25	)
26	LANGUAGE plpgsql
27	SECURITY DEFINER
28	AS $$
29	DECLARE
30	  v_task_id UUID;
31	  v_params JSONB;
32	  v_task_type TEXT;
33	  v_project_id UUID;
34	  v_user_id UUID;
35	  v_status_filter task_status[];
36	  v_worker_model TEXT;
37	  v_has_starving_task BOOLEAN := FALSE;
38	  v_no_matching_tasks BOOLEAN := FALSE;
39	  v_effective_max_task_wait_minutes INT := COALESCE(p_max_task_wait_minutes, 5);
40	BEGIN
41	  -- Set status filter based on include_active flag
42	  IF p_include_active THEN
43	    v_status_filter := ARRAY['Queued'::task_status, 'In Progress'::task_status];
44	  ELSE
45	    v_status_filter := ARRAY['Queued'::task_status];
46	  END IF;
47	
48	  -- Get worker's current model for affinity matching
49	  SELECT current_model INTO v_worker_model
50	  FROM workers
51	  WHERE id = p_worker_id AND status = 'active';
52	
53	  -- Compute eligible users once and reuse for both starvation check and claim query
54	  CREATE TEMP TABLE _eligible_users ON COMMIT DROP AS
55	    SELECT
56	      u.id as user_id,
57	      u.credits,
58	      COALESCE((u.settings->'ui'->'generationMethods'->>'inCloud')::boolean, true) as allows_cloud,
59	      COUNT(in_progress_tasks.id) as in_progress_count
60	    FROM users u
61	    LEFT JOIN projects p ON p.user_id = u.id
62	    LEFT JOIN tasks in_progress_tasks ON in_progress_tasks.project_id = p.id
63	      AND in_progress_tasks.status = 'In Progress'::task_status
64	      AND COALESCE(in_progress_tasks.task_type, '') NOT ILIKE '%orchestrator%'
65	    WHERE u.credits > 0
66	      AND COALESCE((u.settings->'ui'->'generationMethods'->>'inCloud')::boolean, true) = true
67	    GROUP BY u.id, u.credits, u.settings
68	    HAVING COUNT(in_progress_tasks.id) < 5;
69	
70	  -- Bypass model affinity when:
71	  -- 1. No matching-model tasks exist (nothing to wait for), OR
72	  -- 2. Any eligible task has waited longer than the max wait threshold (starvation protection)
73	  IF p_same_model_only AND v_worker_model IS NOT NULL THEN
74	    SELECT
75	      NOT bool_or(get_task_model(t.params) = v_worker_model),  -- no matching tasks
76	      bool_or(t.created_at < NOW() - (v_effective_max_task_wait_minutes || ' minutes')::interval)  -- any starving task
77	    INTO v_no_matching_tasks, v_has_starving_task
78	    FROM tasks t
79	    JOIN projects p ON t.project_id = p.id
80	    WHERE t.status = 'Queued'::task_status
81	      AND all_dependencies_complete(t.dependant_on)
82	      AND EXISTS (
83	        SELECT 1 FROM _eligible_users eu WHERE eu.user_id = p.user_id
84	      )
85	      AND (
86	        p_run_type IS NULL OR
87	        get_task_run_type(t.task_type) = p_run_type
88	      );
89	
90	    -- Coalesce NULLs (empty queue = no matching tasks, no starving tasks)
91	    v_no_matching_tasks := COALESCE(v_no_matching_tasks, TRUE);
92	    v_has_starving_task := COALESCE(v_has_starving_task, FALSE);
93	  END IF;
94	
95	  -- Single atomic query to find and claim the next eligible task
96	  WITH ready_tasks AS (
97	    SELECT
98	      t.id,
99	      t.params,
100	      t.task_type,
101	      t.project_id,
102	      t.created_at,
103	      p.user_id,
104	      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
105	        ORDER BY
106	          CASE
107	            WHEN v_has_starving_task OR v_no_matching_tasks THEN NULL
108	            WHEN v_worker_model IS NOT NULL
109	                 AND get_task_model(t.params) = v_worker_model
110	            THEN 0
111	            ELSE 1
112	          END NULLS LAST,
113	          t.created_at ASC
114	      ) as rn
115	    FROM tasks t
116	    JOIN projects p ON t.project_id = p.id
117	    WHERE t.status = 'Queued'::task_status
118	      AND all_dependencies_complete(t.dependant_on)
119	      AND EXISTS (
120	        SELECT 1 FROM _eligible_users eu WHERE eu.user_id = p.user_id
121	      )
122	      AND (
123	        p_run_type IS NULL OR
124	        get_task_run_type(t.task_type) = p_run_type
125	      )
126	      AND (
127	        v_has_starving_task
128	        OR v_no_matching_tasks
129	        OR NOT p_same_model_only
130	        OR v_worker_model IS NULL
131	        OR get_task_model(t.params) = v_worker_model
132	      )
133	  )
134	  UPDATE tasks
135	  SET
136	    status = CASE
137	      WHEN status = 'Queued'::task_status THEN 'In Progress'::task_status
138	      ELSE status
139	    END,
140	    worker_id = CASE
141	      WHEN status = 'Queued'::task_status THEN p_worker_id
142	      ELSE worker_id
143	    END,
144	    updated_at = CASE
145	      WHEN status = 'Queued'::task_status THEN NOW()
146	      ELSE updated_at
147	    END,
148	    generation_started_at = CASE
149	      WHEN status = 'Queued'::task_status THEN NOW()
150	      ELSE generation_started_at
151	    END
152	  FROM ready_tasks rt
153	  WHERE tasks.id = rt.id
154	    AND rt.rn = 1
155	    AND (NOT p_include_active OR tasks.status = 'Queued'::task_status)
156	  RETURNING
157	    tasks.id,
158	    tasks.params,
159	    tasks.task_type,
160	    tasks.project_id,
161	    rt.user_id
162	  INTO v_task_id, v_params, v_task_type, v_project_id, v_user_id;
163	
164	  IF v_task_id IS NOT NULL THEN
165	    task_id := v_task_id;
166	    params := v_params;
167	    task_type := v_task_type;
168	    project_id := v_project_id;
169	    user_id := v_user_id;
170	    RETURN NEXT;
171	  END IF;
172	
173	  RETURN;
174	END;
175	$$;
176	
177	COMMENT ON FUNCTION claim_next_task_service_role(TEXT, BOOLEAN, TEXT, BOOLEAN, INT) IS
178	'Claims next eligible task for service role. Supports multiple dependencies (all must be complete). Prioritizes model affinity until any eligible task exceeds the max wait threshold, then falls back to FIFO. Excludes orchestrators from concurrency limit.';
179	
180	COMMIT;
181
```

Other (or NULL) values preserve current\n--     behavior, except that we also EXCLUDE banodoco_* tasks from non-banodoco\n--     pools so they aren't accidentally claimed by gpu/api workers.\n--\n--   p_task_types TEXT[] DEFAULT NULL\n--     When non-null and non-empty, restricts candidate tasks to those whose\n--     task_type appears in the array. banodoco_* tasks\n-- are no longer eligible for gpu/api workers (which is the correct desired\n-- behavior since those workers can't execute them).\n\nBEGIN;\n\n-- Drop the prior 5-arg overload so we can replace it with the new 7-arg one.\nDROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.claim_next_task_service_role(TEXT, BOOLEAN, TEXT, BOOLEAN, INT);\n\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION claim_next_task_service_role(\n  p_worker_id TEXT,\n  p_include_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,\n  p_run_type TEXT DEFAULT NULL,\n  p_same_model_only BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,\n  p_max_task_wait_minutes INT DEFAULT 5,\n  p_worker_pool TEXT DEFAULT NULL,\n  p_task_types TEXT[] DEFAULT NULL\n)\nRETURNS TABLE(\n  task_id UUID,\n  params JSONB,\n  task_type TEXT,\n  project_id UUID,\n  user_id UUID\n)\nLANGUAGE plpgsql\nSECURITY DEFINER\nAS $$\nDECLARE\n  v_task_id UUID;\n  v_params JSONB;\n  v_task_type TEXT;\n  v_project_id UUID;\n  v_user_id UUID;\n  v_status_filter task_status[];\n  v_worker_model TEXT;\n  v_has_starving_task BOOLEAN := FALSE;\n  v_no_matching_tasks BOOLEAN := FALSE;\n  v_effective_max_task_wait_minutes INT := COALESCE(p_max_task_wait_minutes, 5);\n  v_is_banodoco_pool BOOLEAN := (p_worker_pool = 'banodoco');\n  v_has_task_types_filter BOOLEAN := (p_task_types IS NOT NULL AND array_length(p_task_types, 1) > 0);\nBEGIN\n  -- Set status filter based on include_active flag\n  IF p_include_active THEN\n    v_status_filter := ARRAY['Queued'::task_status, 'In Progress'::task_status];\n  ELSE\n    v_status_filter := ARRAY['Queued'::task_status];\n  END IF;\n\n  -- Get worker's current model for affinity matching\n  SELECT current_model INTO v_worker_model\n  FROM workers\n  WHERE id = p_worker_id AND status = 'active';\n\n  -- Compute eligible users once and reuse for both starvation check and claim query\n  CREATE TEMP TABLE _eligible_users ON COMMIT DROP AS\n    SELECT\n      u.id as user_id,\n      u.credits,\n      COALESCE((u.settings->'ui'->'generationMethods'->>'inCloud')::boolean, true) as allows_cloud,\n      COUNT(in_progress_tasks.id) as in_progress_count\n    FROM users u\n    LEFT JOIN projects p ON p.user_id = u.id\n    LEFT JOIN tasks in_progress_tasks ON in_progress_tasks.project_id = p.id\n      AND in_progress_tasks.status = 'In Progress'::task_status\n      AND COALESCE(in_progress_tasks.task_type, '') NOT ILIKE '%orchestrator%'\n    WHERE u.credits > 0\n      AND COALESCE((u.settings->'ui'->'generationMethods'->>'inCloud')::boolean, true) = true\n    GROUP BY u.id, u.credits, u.settings\n    HAVING COUNT(in_progress_tasks.id) < 5;\n\n  -- Bypass model affinity when:\n  -- 1. No matching-model tasks exist (nothing to wait for), OR\n  -- 2. Any eligible task has waited longer than the max wait threshold (starvation protection)\n  IF p_same_model_only AND v_worker_model IS NOT NULL THEN\n    SELECT\n      NOT bool_or(get_task_model(t.params) = v_worker_model),  -- no matching tasks\n      bool_or(t.created_at < NOW() - (v_effective_max_task_wait_minutes || ' minutes')::interval)  -- any starving task\n    INTO v_no_matching_tasks, v_has_starving_task\n    FROM tasks t\n    JOIN projects p ON t.project_id = p.id\n    WHERE t.status = 'Queued'::task_status\n      AND all_dependencies_complete(t.dependant_on)\n      AND EXISTS (\n        SELECT 1 FROM _eligible_users eu WHERE eu.user_id = p.user_id\n      )\n      AND (\n        p_run_type IS NULL OR\n        get_task_run_type(t.task_type) = p_run_type\n      )\n      AND (\n        -- Banodoco pool: only banodoco_* task types\n        (v_is_banodoco_pool AND t.task_type LIKE 'banodoco\\_%' ESCAPE '\\')\n        OR\n        -- Non-banodoco pool: exclude banodoco_* (they belong to dedicated workers)\n        (NOT v_is_banodoco_pool AND t.task_type NOT LIKE 'banodoco\\_%' ESCAPE '\\')\n      )\n      AND (\n        NOT v_has_task_types_filter\n        OR t.task_type = ANY(p_task_types)\n      );\n\n    -- Coalesce NULLs (empty queue = no matching tasks, no starving tasks)\n    v_no_matching_tasks := COALESCE(v_no_matching_tasks, TRUE);\n    v_has_starving_task := COALESCE(v_has_starving_task, FALSE);\n  END IF;\n\n  -- Single atomic query to find and claim the next eligible task\n  WITH ready_tasks AS (\n    SELECT\n      t.id,\n      t.params,\n      t.task_type,\n      t.project_id,\n      t.created_at,\n      p.user_id,\n      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (\n        ORDER BY\n          CASE\n            WHEN v_has_starving_task OR v_no_matching_tasks THEN NULL\n            WHEN v_worker_model IS NOT NULL\n                 AND get_task_model(t.params) = v_worker_model\n            THEN 0\n            ELSE 1\n          END NULLS LAST,\n          t.created_at ASC\n      ) as rn\n    FROM tasks t\n    JOIN projects p ON t.project_id = p.id\n    WHERE t.status = 'Queued'::task_status\n      AND all_dependencies_complete(t.dependant_on)\n      AND EXISTS (\n        SELECT 1 FROM _eligible_users eu WHERE eu.user_id = p.user_id\n      )\n      AND (\n        p_run_type IS NULL OR\n        get_task_run_type(t.task_type) = p_run_type\n      )\n      AND (\n        -- Banodoco pool: only banodoco_* task types\n        (v_is_banodoco_pool AND t.task_type LIKE 'banodoco\\_%' ESCAPE '\\')\n        OR\n        -- Non-banodoco pool: exclude banodoco_* (dedicated workers handle these)\n        (NOT v_is_banodoco_pool AND t.task_type NOT LIKE 'banodoco\\_%' ESCAPE '\\')\n      )\n      AND (\n        NOT v_has_task_types_filter\n        OR t.task_type = ANY(p_task_types)\n      )\n      AND (\n        v_has_starving_task\n        OR v_no_matching_tasks\n        OR NOT p_same_model_only\n        OR v_worker_model IS NULL\n        OR get_task_model(t.params) = v_worker_model\n      )\n  )\n  UPDATE tasks\n  SET\n    status = CASE\n      WHEN status = 'Queued'::task_status THEN 'In Progress'::task_status\n      ELSE status\n    END,\n    worker_id = CASE\n      WHEN status = 'Queued'::task_status THEN p_worker_id\n      ELSE worker_id\n    END,\n    updated_at = CASE\n      WHEN status = 'Queued'::task_status THEN NOW()\n      ELSE updated_at\n    END,\n    generation_started_at = CASE\n      WHEN status = 'Queued'::task_status THEN NOW()\n      ELSE generation_started_at\n    END\n  FROM ready_tasks rt\n  WHERE tasks.id = rt.id\n    AND rt.rn = 1\n    AND (NOT p_include_active OR tasks.status = 'Queued'::task_status)\n  RETURNING\n    tasks.id,\n    tasks.params,\n    tasks.task_type,\n    tasks.project_id,\n    rt.user_id\n  INTO v_task_id, v_params, v_task_type, v_project_id, v_user_id;\n\n  IF v_task_id IS NOT NULL THEN\n    task_id := v_task_id;\n    params := v_params;\n    task_type := v_task_type;\n    project_id := v_project_id;\n    user_id := v_user_id;\n    RETURN NEXT;\n  END IF;\n\n  RETURN;\nEND;\n$$;\n\nCOMMENT ON FUNCTION claim_next_task_service_role(TEXT, BOOLEAN, TEXT, BOOLEAN, INT, TEXT, TEXT[]) IS\n'Claims next eligible task for service role. Supports worker pools via p_worker_pool (e.g. ''banodoco'' restricts to banodoco_* task_types; other values exclude banodoco_*) and task_type allow-list via p_task_types. Preserves prior behavior for gpu/api callers (which now also no longer accidentally pick up banodoco_* tasks).';\n\nCOMMIT;\n"
```json
}
```

## Report

**Files changed:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/supabase/functions/claim-next-task/index.ts` — +44 / -6 lines. Parses optional `worker_pool` and `task_types` from the body, accepts `'banodoco-worker'` as run_type only when `worker_pool === 'banodoco'`, forwards both new fields into the RPC. Crucially, when run_type is `'banodoco-worker'` we pass `null` for `p_run_type` since the RPC's `get_task_run_type` filter only knows gpu/api — pool/task-type filters take its place.
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/supabase/functions/claim-next-task/index.test.ts` — +137 lines. Added 4 new tests; updated the two existing service-role expectations to include the new RPC params.
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/supabase/migrations/20260504120000_extend_claim_next_task_for_pools.sql` — new file, 221 lines.

**RPC extension needed:** Yes. The latest signature was 5-arg `(TEXT, BOOLEAN, TEXT, BOOLEAN, INT)` from `20260323213000_add_max_task_wait_to_claim.sql`; it had no awareness of pools. The new migration drops it and creates a 7-arg overload adding `p_worker_pool TEXT DEFAULT NULL` and `p_task_types TEXT[] DEFAULT NULL`. When pool is `'banodoco'` only `banodoco_*` task_types qualify; for any other (or null) pool, `banodoco_*` tasks are excluded so gpu/api workers can't accidentally grab them. `p_task_types` is an additive allow-list. The same filter is applied in the starvation pre-check and the main claim CTE.

**Test results:** `npm run test:edge:unit` — 99 files, 546 tests passing (was 542, added 4 banodoco tests). Existing API/GPU paths covered by updated assertions still pass.

**Commit:** `f8599a887` on `sprint-8-themed-render-via-orchestrator`, parented at `ee2e6f10c`. Not pushed.

**Notes / caveats:**
- The migration only affects `claim_next_task_service_role`. PAT path (`claim_next_task_user_pat`) is untouched per the constraint to leave user-token contracts alone.
- Existing 5-arg call sites: there are no other code call sites (the edge function was the only caller, and I updated it). The DROP-then-CREATE means any in-flight Postgres calls during deploy would briefly see the function missing — same pattern as the prior `20260323213000` migration, so consistent with the repo's deploy practice.
- One non-obvious behavior change for gpu/api workers: they now also exclude `banodoco_*` task types. This is desirable (those workers can't execute them), but it is technically a behavior change — flagging in case it's not what you want.
